| RQ-C11-9831 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Upload: Automatic crash upload is opt-in. The runtime must never silently transmit arbitrary application data. | 0827 §602.113 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9832 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — User Consent: Applications may expose a user-controlled policy: CrashUploadPolicy { disabled ask enabled } | 0827 §602.114 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9833 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Recovery Marker: After startup following a crash, the application may query: diagnostics.previous_exit() Possible result: enum PreviousExit { normal crash forced unknown } | 0827 §602.115 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9834 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Previous Crash Artifact: The runtime may expose: diagnostics.previous_crash() which returns metadata, not necessarily the complete artifact. | 0827 §602.116 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9835 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Startup Recovery: On startup: detect incomplete crash artifact ↓ validate ↓ mark finalized ↓ make available | 0827 §602.117 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9836 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Loop Detection: The runtime may maintain a bounded crash-loop counter. Example: application crashes repeatedly ↓ startup counter increases ↓ recovery policy activates Recovery policy belongs primarily to BOOTSTRAP-600/601 and the application lifecycle layer. | 0827 §602.118 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9837 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Loop Diagnostic Event: Example: runtime.crash_loop.detected contains: attempt count last crash ID build ID | 0827 §602.119 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9838 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Assertion and Panic Integration: All fatal paths converge on a common diagnostic mechanism: assert failure ─┐ panic ──────────┤ fatal error ────┼──► fatal diagnostic path native fault ───┤ abort ──────────┘ | 0827 §602.120 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9839 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Native Fault vs Axiom Panic: The diagnostic artifact distinguishes: AXIOM_PANIC NATIVE_FAULT ASSERTION EXPLICIT_ABORT | 0827 §602.121 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9840 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Fatal Exit Code: The runtime should generate a stable internal crash classification. Operating-system exit codes may differ by platform. | 0827 §602.122 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9841 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Platform Adapter: The core API remains platform-neutral. Platform adapters implement: exception capture signal capture stack unwind module enumeration system logging native dump integration | 0827 §602.123 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9842 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Windows Adapter: Supports integration with native Windows exception facilities. Crash artifacts should be able to coexist with native dump tooling. | 0827 §602.124 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9843 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Linux Adapter: Supports: - signals; - native stack state; - ELF module identity; - core-dump-compatible diagnostics. | 0827 §602.125 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9844 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — macOS Adapter: Supports: - native exception/signal mechanisms; - Mach-O module identity; - symbol/debug identity. | 0827 §602.126 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9845 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — iOS Adapter: The runtime must respect platform restrictions. Crash collection must not depend on unrestricted process inspection. Application-generated diagnostics may be stored locally and exported according to platform policy. | 0827 §602.127 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9846 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Android Adapter: The runtime integrates with Android process/native crash facilities where available. Native Axiom crash artifacts remain independently parseable. | 0827 §602.128 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9847 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — WASM Adapter: WASM has no universal native-process crash model. The runtime maps traps and explicit panics into: DiagnosticFault and delegates persistence to the host where required. | 0827 §602.129 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9848 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Source Map / Debug Map: Axiom toolchains may generate: .axsym or equivalent debug artifacts. These map: machine address ↓ function ↓ source file ↓ line | 0827 §602.130 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9849 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Reproducible Diagnostic Identity: Identical source/build inputs should produce identical diagnostic identities where reproducible-build mode is enabled. | 0827 §602.131 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9850 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Non-Reproducible Builds: Build metadata such as timestamps may be excluded from identity computation when reproducibility is requested. | 0827 §602.132 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9851 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Compiler Integration: The compiler emits metadata required for: - event IDs; - source locations; - stack unwinding; - function IDs; - build identity. | 0827 §602.133 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9852 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Linker Integration: The linker combines diagnostic metadata across: object files static libraries dynamic libraries application and preserves module identities. | 0827 §602.134 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9853 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Library Diagnostics: A library must not assume that the host application uses the same logging policy. Libraries should obtain a logger/context from the host. | 0827 §602.135 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9854 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Library Event Namespace: Library events should use a namespace: vendor.library.component or: org.project.component without requiring a central logging service. | 0827 §602.136 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9855 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Runtime Event Namespace: Axiom runtime events use: runtime.* Compiler-generated events use: compiler.* Application events use application-defined namespaces. | 0827 §602.137 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9856 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Event Collision: Event IDs must be scoped by diagnostic namespace or generated through a linker-level allocation mechanism. | 0827 §602.138 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9857 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — User-Defined Diagnostic Types: Axiom permits: struct DiagnosticValue { ... } only when it implements a restricted diagnostic encoding trait. The encoder must have explicit bounded behavior. | 0827 §602.139 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9858 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Arbitrary Display Execution: Logging an object must not invoke an arbitrary unbounded method. The diagnostic encoder contract must define: maximum size maximum recursion maximum execution behavior | 0827 §602.140 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9859 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Recursive Data: Diagnostic serialization detects cycles. Example: A → B → A must not recurse forever. | 0827 §602.141 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9860 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Maximum Diagnostic Depth: Default: max_depth = 8 Configuration may change this within bounded limits. | 0827 §602.142 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9861 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Maximum Event Size: Every event has a maximum encoded size. Example: 64 KiB Events exceeding the limit are truncated or rejected according to policy. | 0827 §602.143 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9862 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Truncation Metadata: Truncated events indicate: truncated = true original_size = N when known. | 0827 §602.144 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9863 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Binary Data: Binary payloads must be bounded. Large buffers should not be logged directly. Instead: log.info("packet", { size: packet.len, hash: hash(packet) }) | 0827 §602.145 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9864 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Hashing: A diagnostic helper may compute: diagnostic_hash(data) to identify repeated payloads without storing the payload. | 0827 §602.146 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9865 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Rate Limiting: High-frequency events may be rate-limited. Example: logger.rate_limit( event = "network.retry", max_events = 100, interval = 1s ) | 0827 §602.147 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9866 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Suppression Summary: Suppressed events should produce a summary: network.retry suppressed=2381 so filtering does not hide the fact that an abnormal volume occurred. | 0827 §602.148 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9867 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Burst Protection: A logger must protect the application from event storms. The diagnostic subsystem itself must not become an outage amplifier. | 0827 §602.149 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9868 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Per-Category Budgets: Applications may define: network: 1 MB/min database: 512 KB/min graphics: 2 MB/min | 0827 §602.150 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9869 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Global Diagnostic Budget: A global budget may cap: bytes events CPU time memory allocated to diagnostics. | 0827 §602.151 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9870 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic CPU Budget: The runtime should expose configuration for limiting expensive formatting/tracing. | 0827 §602.152 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9871 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — High-Frequency Path: For hot loops: if diagnostic.enabled(.trace) { ... } must allow the compiler to hoist or eliminate the check when possible. | 0827 §602.153 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9872 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Compile-Time Category Elimination: If a category is disabled at compile time: log.trace("physics", ...) can become zero instructions. | 0827 §602.154 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9873 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Constant Propagation: Diagnostic configuration should be represented in compiler-visible constants where practical. | 0827 §602.155 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9874 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Link-Time Elimination: Unused diagnostic sinks should be removed by linker dead-code elimination. | 0827 §602.156 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9875 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Hidden Global Initialization Requirement: Axiom diagnostics should use explicit runtime initialization. The runtime may initialize mandatory crash facilities before application entry. | 0827 §602.157 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9876 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Initialization Order: Startup: native process ↓ minimal runtime ↓ crash handler ↓ emergency buffer ↓ diagnostic core ↓ configuration ↓ application | 0827 §602.158 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9877 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Shutdown Order: Shutdown: application ↓ flush logs ↓ flush traces ↓ close exporters ↓ close diagnostic store The crash handler remains available until the process is actually terminating. | 0827 §602.159 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9878 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Abrupt Exit: For: process.exit_now() normal flushing is not guaranteed. The API must document this explicitly. | 0827 §602.160 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9879 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Graceful Exit: For normal shutdown: process.exit() the runtime attempts configured flush operations. | 0827 §602.161 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9880 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Clock: Events contain: wall-clock timestamp monotonic timestamp Wall-clock time is for humans. Monotonic time is for duration ordering. | 0827 §602.162 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9881 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Clock Failure: If wall-clock time is unavailable: timestamp = unknown but monotonic diagnostic ordering remains available. | 0827 §602.163 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9882 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Time Synchronization: The diagnostic subsystem does not assume the wall clock is synchronized. Distributed systems must use trace IDs and monotonic local durations where appropriate. | 0827 §602.164 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9883 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Thread Identity: Thread IDs are captured as native identifiers. The runtime may additionally expose logical task IDs. | 0827 §602.165 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9884 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Task Identity: For async execution: TaskId may be associated with diagnostics. This is especially useful when many tasks share one OS thread. | 0827 §602.166 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9885 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Scheduler Integration: The scheduler may expose: task creation task suspension task resume task completion task failure as trace events. These events are optional. | 0827 §602.167 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9886 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Deadlock Diagnostics: The runtime may provide a diagnostic snapshot of known synchronization state. It must not attempt unsafe lock acquisition from a crash handler. | 0827 §602.168 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9887 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hang Detection: Optional watchdog: application heartbeat ↓ watchdog ↓ no progress ↓ diagnostic snapshot This is not a mandatory crash mechanism. | 0827 §602.169 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9888 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Watchdog Safety: The watchdog must be bounded and must not terminate healthy applications merely because they are intentionally idle. | 0827 §602.170 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9889 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Health API: Applications may expose: trait HealthProvider { fn health() -> HealthStatus } | 0827 §602.171 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9890 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Health Status: enum HealthStatus { healthy degraded unavailable unknown } | 0827 §602.172 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9891 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Health vs Application Health: These are distinct. Diagnostic subsystem health answers: Can diagnostics function? Application health answers: Is the application functioning? | 0827 §602.173 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9892 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Self-Test: Optional: diagnostics.self_test() checks: - ring buffer; - sinks; - storage; - symbol metadata; - crash artifact directory. | 0827 §602.174 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9893 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Self-Test Safety: Self-test must not intentionally trigger an actual process crash. | 0827 §602.175 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9894 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Test Crash Capture: Development builds may expose a controlled test: diagnostics.test_crash() It must be explicitly enabled and unavailable in normal production builds unless intentionally configured. | 0827 §602.176 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9895 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Artifact Naming: Recommended: <AppId>_<BuildId>_<Timestamp>_<CrashId>.axcrash | 0827 §602.177 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9896 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash ID: Each crash receives a locally unique identifier. It must not require network connectivity. | 0827 §602.178 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9897 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — UUID Dependency: The implementation may use UUID-like identifiers but the runtime must not require an external UUID library. | 0827 §602.179 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9898 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Artifact Storage: Default location comes from BOOTSTRAP-601 deployment configuration. The runtime must support platform-appropriate application data directories. | 0827 §602.180 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9899 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Storage Security: Crash artifacts should use restrictive permissions where supported. | 0827 §602.181 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9900 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Storage Quota: Diagnostic storage has a configurable quota. Example: max_total = 128 MB | 0827 §602.182 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9901 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Retention: Retention policy may be: count-based size-based age-based | 0827 §602.183 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9902 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Artifact Corruption Recovery: At startup, incomplete artifacts are: detected validated marked incomplete retained or deleted according to retention policy. | 0827 §602.184 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9903 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Partial Crash Artifact: A partial artifact is still useful. The format therefore supports: complete = false and independently parseable sections. | 0827 §602.185 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9904 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Emergency Artifact Writer: The crash writer should use: preallocated buffers direct/native file APIs fixed-size metadata bounded loops where platform-safe. | 0827 §602.186 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9905 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Writer Failure: If file writing fails: attempt alternate location then: attempt platform-native crash mechanism then terminate. | 0827 §602.187 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9906 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Infinite Recovery: Crash reporting must never repeatedly attempt recovery after fatal corruption. | 0827 §602.188 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9907 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Handler Isolation: The application must not be able to accidentally disable mandatory crash capture through ordinary logger configuration. | 0827 §602.189 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9908 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Permissions: Applications may disable optional diagnostics. They must not be able to violate OS/platform security restrictions. | 0827 §602.190 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9909 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — User Data Policy: The runtime does not automatically inspect arbitrary application memory for crash reporting. Only explicitly defined regions are captured. | 0827 §602.191 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9910 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory Snapshot: Full process-memory dumps are optional and platform-controlled. They are not part of the minimal `.axcrash` requirement. | 0827 §602.192 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9911 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Large Memory Applications: Applications with huge memory footprints must not incur proportional diagnostic overhead during normal operation. | 0827 §602.193 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9912 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Capture Complexity: Target: O(number of captured frames + number of bounded metadata records) No operation should scan the entire heap by default. | 0827 §602.194 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9913 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Normal Logging Complexity: For accepted fixed-size primitive events: O(event_size) For disabled events: O(1) | 0827 §602.195 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9914 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory Requirements: Minimal runtime diagnostics should have bounded memory: emergency crash buffer + configured ring buffers + optional queues No unbounded diagnostic memory structure is permitted. | 0827 §602.196 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9915 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — ABI Stability: Public diagnostic structures intended for native library interoperability must have explicit ABI versions. | 0827 §602.197 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9916 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — C ABI Interoperability: Axiom may expose a minimal C-compatible diagnostic ABI for interoperability. This must not require a C runtime for Axiom applications. | 0827 §602.198 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9917 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Native Callback ABI: Callbacks crossing diagnostic boundaries must declare: calling convention threading contract lifetime error behavior | 0827 §602.199 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9918 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Error Handling: Diagnostic APIs should return explicit errors where an operation can fail. Example: let result = diagnostics.snapshot("support") Possible errors: storage_unavailable quota_exceeded serialization_failed permission_denied busy | 0827 §602.200 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9919 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic API Must Not Panic: Ordinary diagnostic failures should not themselves trigger application panic. Example: logger.flush() must not recursively crash the application merely because disk I/O failed. | 0827 §602.201 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9920 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Recursive Failure Protection: The diagnostic subsystem has a final emergency path: normal diagnostic ↓ failure minimal diagnostic ↓ failure raw termination | 0827 §602.202 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9921 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Acceptance Criteria: BOOTSTRAP-602 is complete when the Axiom implementation can demonstrate: ### Logging - structured logs; - severity levels; - category filtering; - event IDs; - lazy arguments; - compile-time elimination; - bounded events; - thread-safe logging. ### Tracing - trace IDs; - spans; - bounded trace buffers; - sampling; - async-task correlation. ### Crash handling - native fault capture; - panic capture; - assertion capture; - register capture; - bounded stack capture; - module identity; - build identity; - crash artifact generation. ### Security - secret values cannot be logged accidentally; - configuration secrets remain protected; - environment capture is allowlisted; - command-line secrets are not dumped by default. ### Resilience - logger failure does not normally crash the application; - disk-full behavior is bounded; - crash handler does not depend on ordinary heap allocation; - recursive crash handling terminates safely; - partial artifacts remain parseable. ### Toolchain - compiler emits diagnostic metadata; - linker preserves diagnostic identities; - symbols can be matched to crash artifacts; - unused diagnostic components can be dead-stripped. ### Platform At minimum, the architecture must support: Windows Linux macOS iOS Android WASM through platform adapters. | 0827 §602.203 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9922 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Required Compiler/Runtime Components: Implementation should produce: axiom.diagnostics.core axiom.diagnostics.logging axiom.diagnostics.trace axiom.diagnostics.crash axiom.diagnostics.symbols axiom.diagnostics.storage axiom.diagnostics.export These are logical components, not necessarily separate binaries. | 0827 §602.204 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9923 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Required Tooling: The Axiom toolchain should provide: ax log ax crash ax symbolize ax diagnose ax dump Possible operations: ax crash inspect file.axcrash ax symbolize file.axcrash ax diagnose build/ | 0827 §602.205 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9924 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax crash inspect`: Displays: application build platform fault thread stack modules recent logs trace checkpoint configuration fingerprint | 0827 §602.206 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9925 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax symbolize`: Consumes: .axcrash .axsym and produces source-level stack information. | 0827 §602.207 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9926 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax crash export`: Converts: .axcrash to: JSON text diagnostic package without changing the original artifact. | 0827 §602.208 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9927 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax diagnose`: Can analyze: - crash artifacts; - logs; - trace data; - build metadata; - symbol files. It should remain a toolchain feature rather than part of the application runtime. | 0827 §602.209 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9928 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — AI-Friendly Diagnostics: Axiom diagnostic artifacts should be machine-readable. The canonical structured representation must expose: stable IDs schema versions explicit types source locations build identity causal relationships This allows AI tooling to reason over failures without relying exclusively on human-formatted logs. | 0827 §602.210 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9929 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Causality: Events may reference: parent event trace span request task checkpoint This enables reconstruction such as: request ↓ task ↓ database query ↓ timeout ↓ retry ↓ panic ↓ crash | 0827 §602.211 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9930 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Failure Chain: The diagnostic runtime may assign: FailureId to related failures. Example: FailureId = F-1827 All related events can reference the same failure. | 0827 §602.212 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9931 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Error Context: Axiom errors may optionally carry: struct ErrorContext { error_code source cause trace_id span_id } | 0827 §602.213 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9932 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Error Cause Chain: Errors may form: application error ↓ database error ↓ network error ↓ OS error The chain must be bounded. | 0827 §602.214 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9933 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cause Depth: Default maximum: 16 to prevent pathological recursive error chains. | 0827 §602.215 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9934 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Serialization: Error chains can be serialized into crash artifacts and snapshots. Secrets remain filtered. | 0827 §602.216 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9935 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Runtime Version Compatibility: Diagnostic readers should support multiple artifact versions where practical. The artifact format must explicitly identify its version. | 0827 §602.217 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9936 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Schema Migration: Axiom tooling may migrate: .axcrash v1 to a newer logical representation without modifying the original artifact. | 0827 §602.218 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9937 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Long-Term Preservation: Crash artifacts must be interpretable even if the original application is no longer installed. Therefore the artifact must contain enough metadata to identify: format platform architecture build runtime module identities | 0827 §602.219 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9938 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Mandatory Cloud: Axiom's diagnostics architecture is fully functional without: cloud vendor account telemetry server internet | 0827 §602.220 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9939 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Mandatory Third-Party Runtime: The final native executable must not require an external logging or crash-reporting runtime merely to execute. | 0827 §602.221 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9940 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Determinism: Diagnostic behavior must be deterministic with respect to: - filtering; - event schema; - artifact encoding; - retention policy. Timestamps and runtime scheduling are naturally nondeterministic. | 0827 §602.222 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9941 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Performance Target: The target for disabled logging: effectively zero runtime overhead when compile-time elimination is possible. For enabled primitive logging: bounded O(event_size) with no mandatory heap allocation. | 0827 §602.223 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9942 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Performance: Crash capture must prioritize: safety > completeness > convenience The runtime must prefer a partial valid crash artifact over risking recursive failure while attempting a perfect one. | 0827 §602.224 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9943 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Relationship to BOOTSTRAP-600: BOOTSTRAP-600 owns: application state session checkpoint recovery crash-resilient state BOOTSTRAP-602 only records diagnostic references to that state. It must not become the state-management subsystem. | 0827 §602.225 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9944 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Relationship to BOOTSTRAP-601: BOOTSTRAP-601 owns: configuration profiles environment secrets deployment identity BOOTSTRAP-602 consumes safe identifiers from it. It must not duplicate configuration resolution. | 0827 §602.226 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9945 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Boundary Rule: The three subsystems therefore remain: 600 = What state does the application have? 601 = How is the application configured/deployed? 602 = What happened while the application was running? This separation is mandatory. | 0827 §602.227 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9946 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Architectural Result: After BOOTSTRAP-602, a native Axiom application has a complete foundational observability path: APPLICATION │ ┌─────────┼─────────┐ ▼         ▼         ▼ STATE      CONFIG   DIAGNOSTICS 600        601        602 │          │          │ └──────────┼──────────┘ ▼ BUILD IDENTITY │ ▼ FAILURE EVIDENCE │ ┌──────────┼───────────┐ ▼          ▼           ▼ LOGS       TRACE       CRASH │          │           │ └──────────┼───────────┘ ▼ .AXCRASH / STORE This creates the minimum native foundation required for an Axiom application to be diagnosable in production without depending on third-party infrastructure. | 0827 §602.228 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9947 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Task Completion: **BOOTSTRAP-602 is complete.** The specification now establishes: - native structured logging; - compile-time log elimination; - runtime filtering; - structured diagnostic events; - trace/span infrastructure; - crash-safe emergency buffers; - native fault capture; - panic/assertion diagnostics; - stack/register/module capture; - symbol identity; - `.axcrash` artifact architecture; - privacy and secret protection; - configuration/state correlation; - bounded logging and tracing; - diagnostic snapshots; - health/watchdog foundations; - platform adapters; - compiler/linker integration; - AI-readable diagnostic metadata; - offline-first operation; - no mandatory third-party runtime dependency. **Next task: `BOOTSTRAP-603 — NATIVE APPLICATION SECURITY, IDENTITY, CAPABILITY & TRUST RUNTIME 5.0`** .: BOOTSTRAP-602 đã nối đúng sau 601. Chuỗi tiếp theo là **BOOTSTRAP-603**, không cần thay đổi số thứ tự hay quay lại các task trước. | 0827 §602.229 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9948 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Purpose: BOOTSTRAP-603 defines the foundational security model of Axiom applications. The subsystem governs: 1. application identity; 2. execution identity; 3. capabilities; 4. resource permissions; 5. trust boundaries; 6. privilege boundaries; 7. secure handles; 8. cryptographic primitives; 9. secure randomness; 10. credential isolation; 11. process and module trust; 12. sandbox integration; 13. permission requests; 14. authorization decisions; 15. security auditing; 16. secure IPC boundaries; 17. platform security adapters; 18. secure failure behavior. The design must avoid turning Axiom into a complicated security framework. The fundamental rule is: > **Code should possess authority explicitly rather than receiving unlimited authority implicitly.** | 0828 §603.0 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9949 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Principles: Axiom security follows: least privilege explicit authority deny by default capability-oriented access immutable identity bounded resources secure failure auditable decisions platform integration no mandatory cloud | 0828 §603.1 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9950 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Implicit Universal Authority: An ordinary Axiom application must not automatically receive unrestricted access to: - filesystem; - network; - processes; - devices; - credentials; - environment; - system configuration. Access must come from the platform or an explicitly declared capability. | 0828 §603.2 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9951 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Model: The primary abstraction is: Capability<T> A capability represents authority to perform a specific class of operation. Example: Capability<FileSystem> Capability<Network> Capability<Camera> Capability<Process> Possessing the capability is the authorization. | 0828 §603.3 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9952 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Is Not a String: This is forbidden as the primary authorization mechanism: if permissions.contains("filesystem.write") { ... } Instead: fn save(file: FileWriteCapability, data: Bytes) The type system carries authority. | 0828 §603.4 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9953 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Non-Forgery: Application code must not be able to construct an arbitrary privileged capability. For example: Capability<FileSystem>() is invalid unless the compiler/runtime provides a legitimate authority source. | 0828 §603.5 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9954 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Origin: A capability originates from: platform application manifest parent capability user authorization secure subsystem trusted bootstrap | 0828 §603.6 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9955 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Attenuation: A capability may be restricted. Example: let full = filesystem let images = full.subtree("/images") The resulting capability has no authority outside `/images`. | 0828 §603.7 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9956 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Monotonicity: Deriving a child capability must never increase authority. child.authority ⊆ parent.authority This is a core invariant. | 0828 §603.8 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9957 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Revocation: Capabilities may be revocable. capability.revoke() A revoked capability must fail future operations. Already completed operations are not retroactively undone. | 0828 §603.9 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9958 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Lifetime: Capabilities are ordinary native values with explicit lifetime. They do not require garbage collection. | 0828 §603.10 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9959 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Transfer: A capability can be transferred between trusted execution contexts if the API explicitly allows it. Example: worker.send(capability) The sender may optionally relinquish its authority. | 0828 §603.11 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9960 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Duplication: Duplication policy depends on capability type. Some capabilities may be: copyable shareable move-only non-transferable | 0828 §603.12 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9961 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Move-Only Security Capabilities: Highly privileged capabilities should support move semantics: let cap2 = move cap1 After transfer: cap1 = invalid cap2 = valid | 0828 §603.13 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9962 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Scope: Capabilities may be scoped to: application process thread task session resource operation | 0828 §603.14 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9963 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Resource Capability: A resource capability may represent: file directory socket device process memory region IPC endpoint credential cryptographic key | 0828 §603.15 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9964 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — File Capability: Example: FileReadCapability FileWriteCapability DirectoryCapability Read and write authority are separate. | 0828 §603.16 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9965 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Path Authority: A file capability should preferably contain a canonicalized authority boundary rather than repeatedly trusting arbitrary path strings. | 0828 §603.17 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9966 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Path Traversal Protection: A capability restricted to: /app/data must not permit: /app/data/../secrets to escape its authority. Canonicalization occurs before authorization. | 0828 §603.18 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9967 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Symlink / Reparse Boundaries: Platform-specific path mechanisms such as: - symbolic links; - junctions; - reparse points; must not silently bypass a capability boundary. The runtime adapter must define secure resolution semantics. | 0828 §603.19 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9968 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — File Operation API: Preferred: file = fs.open(capability, relative_path) rather than: file = open("/arbitrary/path") for sandboxed applications. | 0828 §603.20 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9969 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Network Capability: Network authority is explicit. Possible forms: NetworkConnectCapability NetworkListenCapability NetworkDnsCapability | 0828 §603.21 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9970 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Network Attenuation: A network capability may be restricted by: protocol host port address family direction Example: let api = network.connect_to("api.example.com", 443) | 0828 §603.22 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9971 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — DNS Authority: DNS access may be separated from raw socket authority. This permits tighter sandboxing. | 0828 §603.23 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9972 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Process Capability: Process authority includes: spawn inspect signal terminate debug These are separate capabilities. | 0828 §603.24 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9973 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Process Spawning: Axiom should not expose unrestricted shell execution as the normal process API. Preferred: process.spawn( executable, arguments, capability ) | 0828 §603.25 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9974 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Shell Independence: The runtime must not require: cmd.exe powershell /bin/sh /bin/bash to launch ordinary processes. | 0828 §603.26 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9975 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Argument Safety: Process arguments are passed as structured argument arrays. The runtime must not concatenate them into a shell command string. | 0828 §603.27 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9976 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Environment Inheritance: Environment inheritance must be explicit. Example: process.spawn( env = environment.minimal() ) | 0828 §603.28 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9977 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Credential Capability: Credentials are represented as opaque values. Example: Credential<T> They must not automatically convert to: String Bytes DiagnosticValue | 0828 §603.29 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9978 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secret Integration: BOOTSTRAP-601 `Secret<T>` remains the configuration/secret representation. BOOTSTRAP-603 defines runtime authority for using the secret. | 0828 §603.30 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9979 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secret Access: A secret should be accessed through a restricted operation: secret.with_value(/value/ { use(value) }) This allows future implementations to minimize exposure. | 0828 §603.31 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9980 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secret Memory: Sensitive memory may require: non-swappable memory zeroization restricted copying when supported by the platform and appropriate for the secret class. | 0828 §603.32 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9981 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Zeroization: API: secure.zeroize(buffer) The compiler must prevent optimization from removing a required security wipe. | 0828 §603.33 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9982 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secret Copying: The runtime should discourage unnecessary copies of secret data. The type system may mark sensitive values as: move-only non-copyable | 0828 §603.34 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9983 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cryptographic Boundary: Axiom provides cryptographic primitives as native runtime facilities. However, application-level protocols must not be silently invented by the runtime. | 0828 §603.35 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9984 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cryptographic API Categories: Core categories: hash MAC KDF AEAD signature key generation randomness constant-time comparison | 0828 §603.36 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9985 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hash API: Example: hash.sha256(data) The API returns a fixed-size digest type. | 0828 §603.37 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9986 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Typed Digest: Example: Digest<sha256> rather than a generic untyped byte array. | 0828 §603.38 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9987 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — MAC: Example: mac.hmac_sha256(key, data) Keys remain opaque. | 0828 §603.39 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9988 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — KDF: Supported conceptual interface: kdf.derive( key, salt, context, output_length ) | 0828 §603.40 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9989 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — AEAD: Authenticated encryption provides: aead.encrypt(key, nonce, plaintext, associated_data) aead.decrypt(key, nonce, ciphertext, associated_data) Decryption failure must not expose partially authenticated plaintext. | 0828 §603.41 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9990 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Nonce Handling: Nonce rules must be explicit. The runtime must provide safe nonce generation where the algorithm requires uniqueness/randomness. | 0828 §603.42 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9991 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Signature API: Example: signature.sign(private_key, data) signature.verify(public_key, data, signature) | 0828 §603.43 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9992 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Key Types: Keys must be strongly typed: PrivateKey<Algorithm> PublicKey<Algorithm> SymmetricKey<Algorithm> | 0828 §603.44 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9993 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Algorithm Agility: The API must identify algorithms explicitly. Avoid: encrypt(data) where the algorithm is hidden. Prefer: aead.encrypt(.AES256_GCM, ...) or an equivalent typed key API. | 0828 §603.45 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9994 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cryptographic Primitive Policy: The runtime must distinguish: available algorithm approved algorithm legacy algorithm insecure algorithm Applications should receive explicit diagnostics when using deprecated primitives. | 0828 §603.46 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9995 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Randomness: API: random.secure(bytes) must use the platform's cryptographically secure random source. | 0828 §603.47 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9996 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — General Randomness: A separate API: random.fast() may exist for simulation and non-security workloads. It must not be advertised as cryptographically secure. | 0828 §603.48 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9997 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Random Type Separation: Security-sensitive APIs should reject ordinary pseudo-random generators where secure randomness is required. | 0828 §603.49 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9998 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Constant-Time Comparison: API: secure.equals(a, b) provides comparison suitable for sensitive byte sequences. | 0828 §603.50 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-9999 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Timing Resistance: The runtime should avoid obvious early-exit behavior for cryptographic comparisons. The exact guarantees are platform/compiler dependent and must be documented. | 0828 §603.51 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10000 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Key Lifecycle: Keys have explicit states: generated active suspended revoked destroyed | 0828 §603.52 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10001 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Key Destruction: Destroying a key must invalidate its capability and, where possible, clear sensitive memory. | 0828 §603.53 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10002 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hardware-Backed Keys: The architecture supports opaque references to platform key stores. Examples: TPM Secure Enclave Android Keystore platform credential store The core runtime must not assume any particular hardware exists. | 0828 §603.54 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10003 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hardware Key Abstraction: HardwareKey<Algorithm> can expose permitted cryptographic operations without exposing raw key material. | 0828 §603.55 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10004 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trust Identity: An application has: AppIdentity containing: application_id publisher_id build_id platform_identity | 0828 §603.56 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10005 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Application ID: The application ID is stable across builds of the same logical application. | 0828 §603.57 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10006 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Build ID: The build ID identifies a particular executable build. This integrates with BOOTSTRAP-602 diagnostics. | 0828 §603.58 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10007 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Publisher Identity: A publisher identity identifies the signing authority or development authority associated with an application. | 0828 §603.59 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10008 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Signing Identity: A signed build may contain: publisher certificate/key identity signature metadata build identity The runtime can expose this information without requiring a network lookup. | 0828 §603.60 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10009 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Code Signing: Axiom toolchains should support platform-native code-signing formats. The compiler itself does not need to implement every external signing service. | 0828 §603.61 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10010 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Signature Verification: API: trust.verify_signature(binary, public_key) returns a structured result. | 0828 §603.62 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10011 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trust Result: enum TrustStatus { trusted untrusted invalid unknown } These are descriptive security states, not political or subjective judgments. | 0828 §603.63 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10012 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trust Chain: A verification result may include: root intermediate leaf artifact and failure reason. | 0828 §603.64 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10013 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Automatic Trust of Local Files: A local executable is not automatically trusted merely because it exists on disk. | 0828 §603.65 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10014 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Module Identity: Each native module may expose: ModuleId BuildId PublisherId SignatureStatus | 0828 §603.66 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10015 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dynamic Library Loading: Dynamic loading requires an explicit capability in restricted environments. | 0828 §603.67 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10016 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Library Trust Policy: An application may require: loader.require_publisher(PublisherId) or: loader.require_signature(...) before loading a module. | 0828 §603.68 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10017 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dependency Verification: A deployment manifest may specify expected: module ID version hash publisher | 0828 §603.69 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10018 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dependency Mismatch: A mismatch should produce a structured security error. The runtime must not silently substitute an unrelated module. | 0828 §603.70 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10019 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hash Verification: Example: module.require_hash(expected) This protects against unexpected binary replacement. | 0828 §603.71 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10020 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — TOCTOU Protection: Security-sensitive resource access must minimize: check ↓ resource changes ↓ use windows. Where platform APIs support atomic secure operations, the runtime should use them. | 0828 §603.72 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10021 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Handle: Axiom uses opaque handles for privileged native resources: Handle<T> The numeric native handle is not directly exposed by default. | 0828 §603.73 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10022 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Handle Ownership: Handles have explicit ownership: owned borrowed shared invalid This should integrate with Axiom's broader resource/lifetime model without introducing a mandatory borrow checker. | 0828 §603.74 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10023 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Handle Closing: Example: with fs.open(cap, "data.bin") as file { ... } leaves scope and closes the handle deterministically. | 0828 §603.75 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10024 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No GC Requirement: Security-sensitive resource cleanup must not depend on garbage collection. | 0828 §603.76 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10025 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Double Close: Closing an owned resource twice is invalid. Debug builds should detect it. Release behavior should be deterministic and safe. | 0828 §603.77 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10026 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Tokens: Internally, capabilities may be represented using: opaque pointer native handle index kernel token sealed structure The representation is platform-specific. | 0828 §603.78 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10027 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Forgery Resistance: The representation must make accidental or ordinary application-level forgery impractical. | 0828 §603.79 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10028 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory Safety Boundary: The security runtime does not replace Axiom's memory model. Instead it defines privileged-resource boundaries independent of whether the application uses: - stack values; - owned values; - flat memory; - native handles; - shared memory. | 0828 §603.80 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10029 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unsafe Code: Axiom may provide: unsafe { ... } for low-level operations. Unsafe code does not automatically gain all capabilities. | 0828 §603.81 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10030 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unsafe ≠ Privileged: This distinction is mandatory: unsafe ≠ authorized Unsafe code can violate memory/type invariants within its authority, but cannot manufacture platform permissions. | 0828 §603.82 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10031 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Boundaries and FFI: An FFI call inherits only the capabilities explicitly passed to it. Calling native code does not grant universal Axiom authority. | 0828 §603.83 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10032 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Native ABI Boundary: FFI interfaces should declare security requirements. Example: extern fn camera_capture( camera: CameraCapability ) | 0828 §603.84 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10033 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — IPC Capability: IPC endpoints are represented as: IpcCapability<T> | 0828 §603.85 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10034 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — IPC Authentication: An IPC endpoint may authenticate the peer using: process identity application identity publisher identity session identity cryptographic identity platform identity | 0828 §603.86 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10035 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — IPC Authorization: Authentication answers: Who are you? Authorization answers: What are you allowed to do? Axiom must keep these concepts separate. | 0828 §603.87 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10036 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Peer Identity: struct PeerIdentity { app_id publisher_id process_id session_id } Fields vary by platform. | 0828 §603.88 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10037 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure IPC Handshake: A secure channel may establish: peer identity channel identity capabilities session key | 0828 §603.89 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10038 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Passing over IPC: A trusted process may explicitly transfer authority through IPC. The receiver receives only the transferred capability. | 0828 §603.90 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10039 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Revocation over IPC: Revocation must propagate to transferred capabilities where the platform supports centralized capability tracking. | 0828 §603.91 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10040 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Sandboxing: Axiom applications may declare a sandbox profile. Example: filesystem.read network.connect camera microphone gpu process.spawn | 0828 §603.92 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10041 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Manifest Integration: BOOTSTRAP-601 deployment manifests may declare required capabilities. Example: capabilities: filesystem: read: app_data network: connect: api.example.com:443 | 0828 §603.93 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10042 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Manifest vs Runtime: Manifest declaration expresses: what the application requests Runtime capability expresses: what the application actually possesses They are distinct. | 0828 §603.94 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10043 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Denial: If a requested capability is denied: CapabilityError.denied is returned. | 0828 §603.95 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10044 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Silent Escalation: The runtime must never automatically retry a denied capability using a more privileged mechanism. | 0828 §603.96 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10045 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — User Permission: Interactive permissions may involve the user or operating system. The runtime exposes the result: permission.request(camera) without deciding whether the user should grant it. | 0828 §603.97 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10046 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Permission State: enum PermissionState { granted denied restricted unavailable unknown } | 0828 §603.98 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10047 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Permission Revocation: Applications must handle permissions disappearing after they were previously granted. | 0828 §603.99 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10048 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Permission Cache: The runtime may cache permission state briefly but must not assume permanent authorization. | 0828 §603.100 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10049 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Defaults: Default policy: no capability unless explicitly granted by platform/runtime. | 0828 §603.101 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10050 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Development Mode: Development builds may request broader capabilities, but development mode must not silently weaken production security. | 0828 §603.102 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10051 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Debugger Capability: Debugging another process is a privileged capability. It must be separate from ordinary process inspection. | 0828 §603.103 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10052 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory Inspection: Reading another process's memory requires explicit authorization. The runtime must not provide unrestricted memory inspection as a normal API. | 0828 §603.104 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10053 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Code Injection: Dynamic code injection is not a normal Axiom capability. If a platform/debugging environment supports it, it belongs to explicitly privileged tooling. | 0828 §603.105 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10054 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dynamic Code Loading: Runtime-generated executable code must be controlled by the execution/security layer. A normal application cannot silently convert arbitrary writable memory into executable code. | 0828 §603.106 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10055 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — W^X: Where the platform supports it, executable memory should follow: write OR execute rather than: write AND execute simultaneously. | 0828 §603.107 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10056 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — JIT Capability: JIT execution is a separate capability: Capability<JitExecution> This is especially relevant for: - scripting; - dynamic compilation; - GPU kernels; - runtime code generation. | 0828 §603.108 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10057 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Executable Memory: The runtime should expose controlled allocation: exec_memory.allocate(capability, size) with explicit permission transitions. | 0828 §603.109 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10058 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory Protection: Memory regions may transition: read/write read-only read/execute according to platform constraints. | 0828 §603.110 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10059 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Guard Pages: Security-sensitive native allocations may use guard pages where practical. | 0828 §603.111 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10060 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Stack Protection: The toolchain should support platform stack-protection mechanisms where appropriate. | 0828 §603.112 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10061 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Integer Overflow Policy: The security runtime does not redefine Axiom arithmetic semantics. However, security-sensitive code should have explicit checked arithmetic APIs. Example: checked.add(a, b) | 0828 §603.113 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10062 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Bounds Validation: Native APIs must validate: length offset count alignment handle state before unsafe operations. | 0828 §603.114 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10063 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Integer-to-Size Conversion: Conversions into native allocation/index sizes must provide checked forms. | 0828 §603.115 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10064 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Serialization Security: Binary deserialization must enforce: maximum size maximum depth maximum collection count maximum string size | 0828 §603.116 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10065 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Arbitrary Deserialization Code: Deserializing external data must not execute arbitrary constructors or methods. | 0828 §603.117 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10066 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Parser Isolation: Security-sensitive parsers should operate with bounded resource budgets. | 0828 §603.118 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10067 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Resource Exhaustion: Capabilities may include quotas: max file size max network bytes max processes max memory max CPU max IPC messages | 0828 §603.119 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10068 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Quota Model: CapabilityQuota { bytes operations duration concurrency } | 0828 §603.120 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10069 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Quota Enforcement: A quota violation returns: SecurityError.quota_exceeded rather than silently truncating a security-sensitive operation. | 0828 §603.121 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10070 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Rate-Limited Capabilities: Capabilities may enforce operation rates. Example: 100 requests/minute | 0828 §603.122 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10071 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Events: Security-sensitive decisions should integrate with BOOTSTRAP-602: security.capability.granted security.capability.denied security.permission.changed security.signature.invalid security.module.rejected security.credential.access | 0828 §603.123 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10072 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Privacy: Audit events must not expose: - passwords; - private keys; - raw access tokens; - secret configuration values. | 0828 §603.124 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10073 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Integrity: High-security deployments may require tamper-evident audit records. This can use chained hashes: H(event_n // H(event_n-1)) | 0828 §603.125 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10074 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Storage: Audit logs remain separate from ordinary application logs. This prevents normal log rotation from accidentally destroying security records. | 0828 §603.126 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10075 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Event Severity: Security events use ordinary BOOTSTRAP-602 severity levels but may additionally carry a security classification. | 0828 §603.127 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10076 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Classification: Example: enum SecurityEventClass { authentication authorization capability integrity credential sandbox cryptography } | 0828 §603.128 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10077 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Authentication API: The core runtime provides primitives for authenticating identities but does not mandate a universal account system. | 0828 §603.129 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10078 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Identity Provider: An application may integrate: IdentityProvider which returns an opaque identity. | 0828 §603.130 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10079 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Identity Object: Identity { id issuer attributes } Attributes must be explicitly typed and bounded. | 0828 §603.131 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10080 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Authentication Result: enum AuthenticationResult { authenticated rejected unavailable expired invalid } | 0828 §603.132 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10081 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Authorization: Authorization is capability-based by default. Role-based or attribute-based systems may be implemented above the primitive capability layer. | 0828 §603.133 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10082 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Role Mapping: An application may map: identity ↓ role ↓ capability set but the runtime should ultimately enforce concrete capabilities. | 0828 §603.134 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10083 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Session Identity: BOOTSTRAP-600 session state may expose: SessionIdentity for diagnostics and authorization. | 0828 §603.135 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10084 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Session Separation: Authentication credentials and session state must not be conflated. | 0828 §603.136 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10085 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Token Handling: Tokens should be represented as opaque types: AccessToken RefreshToken SessionToken rather than generic strings. | 0828 §603.137 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10086 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Token Logging: Token types are automatically protected from BOOTSTRAP-602 logging. | 0828 §603.138 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10087 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Token Equality: Security-sensitive token comparison uses constant-time comparison where applicable. | 0828 §603.139 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10088 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Expiration: Security credentials may expose: expires_at() without exposing secret contents. | 0828 §603.140 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10089 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Clock Security: Expiration checks should account for clock manipulation where the platform provides monotonic or trusted time sources. | 0828 §603.141 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10090 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trust Store: The runtime may provide access to platform trust stores through: TrustStore without exposing platform-specific internals. | 0828 §603.142 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10091 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Certificate Object: Certificates are parsed into typed structures. Malformed certificates return structured errors. | 0828 §603.143 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10092 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Certificate Validation: Validation may check: signature chain validity period key usage hostname policy revocation status depending on the requested operation. | 0828 §603.144 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10093 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hostname Validation: TLS-like network clients must not treat certificate-chain validity alone as hostname authorization. | 0828 §603.145 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10094 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — TLS Boundary: Axiom may provide secure network transports. The application API should make certificate and hostname validation the normal behavior. | 0828 §603.146 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10095 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Plaintext Transport: Plaintext networking remains possible for explicitly non-sensitive protocols. Security-sensitive APIs should not silently downgrade to plaintext. | 0828 §603.147 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10096 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Downgrade Protection: A secure connection should not automatically downgrade after: certificate failure authentication failure protocol mismatch without an explicit application policy. | 0828 §603.148 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10097 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cryptographic Failure: Cryptographic verification failure must return a failure result. It must not be converted into a warning and continued silently. | 0828 §603.149 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10098 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Error Messages: Errors should explain enough for debugging without revealing secrets. Example: authentication failed rather than: password hash for user X was ... | 0828 §603.150 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10099 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Error Redaction: Security errors are automatically safe for BOOTSTRAP-602 diagnostic serialization. | 0828 §603.151 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10100 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Panic Safety: A security failure must not cause a panic merely because the capability was denied. | 0828 §603.152 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10101 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Privilege Boundary: Privilege escalation is represented explicitly: security.request_privilege(...) The runtime cannot silently elevate. | 0828 §603.153 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10102 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Privileged Helper: Some platforms may require a privileged helper process. The helper must have: minimal capability set authenticated IPC explicit protocol bounded input | 0828 §603.154 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10103 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Helper Authentication: The main process must authenticate the helper before sending sensitive operations. | 0828 §603.155 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10104 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Helper Authorization: The helper must authenticate the requesting application before accepting privileged operations. | 0828 §603.156 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10105 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Confused Deputy Prevention: A privileged helper must not blindly perform arbitrary operations requested by any client. Every request must be authorized against the caller's identity and granted capability. | 0828 §603.157 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10106 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Delegation: A process may delegate a restricted capability: parent ↓ child but delegation cannot exceed the parent's authority. | 0828 §603.158 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10107 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Child Process Security: When spawning a child process, the parent may specify: capabilities environment filesystem network handles working directory resource quotas | 0828 §603.159 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10108 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Default Child Authority: A child process receives no additional authority merely because the parent possesses it. | 0828 §603.160 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10109 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Inheritance: Inheritance must be explicit. Example: spawn(..., inherit = [.stdin, .stdout]) | 0828 §603.161 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10110 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Handle Inheritance: Native handle inheritance is disabled by default where platform semantics allow. | 0828 §603.162 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10111 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Temporary Capabilities: Some capabilities may have expiration: capability.until(deadline) | 0828 §603.163 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10112 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Time-Bounded Authority: After expiration: operation → denied | 0828 §603.164 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10113 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — One-Shot Capabilities: Some authority can be consumed once: OneShotCapability<T> Useful for: - secure handoff; - installation tokens; - one-time secrets. | 0828 §603.165 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10114 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Audit Identity: Every capability may have an opaque identifier for diagnostics: CapabilityId This identifier does not expose the capability's secret material. | 0828 §603.166 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10115 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Context: The runtime maintains a security context: SecurityContext { app_identity session_identity capabilities trust } | 0828 §603.167 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10116 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Context Propagation: Async tasks inherit only the security context explicitly configured for them. | 0828 §603.168 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10117 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Context Isolation: A child task may receive a reduced security context. | 0828 §603.169 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10118 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Ambient Privilege Leakage: A task created from a privileged context must not accidentally become globally privileged. | 0828 §603.170 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10119 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Thread Context: Thread-local storage may cache security context, but the authoritative capability state remains explicit and revocable. | 0828 §603.171 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10120 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — FFI Security Review Boundary: Any API declared: extern should identify whether it: reads files opens network executes code accesses devices uses credentials where this can be represented statically. | 0828 §603.172 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10121 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Native Module Manifest: Native modules may declare: required_capabilities provided_capabilities security_level publisher | 0828 §603.173 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10122 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Module Loading Policy: The application may require: signed module approved publisher expected hash expected ABI expected version before loading. | 0828 §603.174 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10123 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — ABI Trust: ABI compatibility is distinct from security trust. A compatible module is not automatically a trusted module. | 0828 §603.175 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10124 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Update: The architecture supports signed application updates. Update process: download ↓ verify signature ↓ verify identity ↓ verify compatibility ↓ stage ↓ activate | 0828 §603.176 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10125 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Atomic Update: Where platform support exists, activation should be atomic. A failed update must leave the previous known-good installation intact. | 0828 §603.177 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10126 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Rollback: The deployment layer may maintain: current previous candidate versions. Security metadata must accompany each version. | 0828 §603.178 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10127 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Update Trust: A newer version must not automatically be trusted merely because it is newer. The signing/trust policy must still pass. | 0828 §603.179 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10128 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Bootstrap: At startup: platform ↓ executable identity ↓ signature/trust policy ↓ runtime initialization ↓ capability establishment ↓ application | 0828 §603.180 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10129 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Bootstrap Failure: If mandatory integrity verification fails: application startup = denied rather than continuing in a partially trusted state. | 0828 §603.181 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10130 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic Integration: BOOTSTRAP-602 records: build ID publisher ID module identity capability denials trust failures security events but never raw secrets. | 0828 §603.182 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10131 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Integration: BOOTSTRAP-602 crash artifacts may contain: security context identifier trust status active capability class but not capability secrets. | 0828 §603.183 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10132 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Configuration Integration: BOOTSTRAP-601 declares requested capabilities. BOOTSTRAP-603 determines actual authority. | 0828 §603.184 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10133 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — State Integration: BOOTSTRAP-600 may persist: permission state security migration state session identity references but sensitive credentials remain in the secure credential subsystem. | 0828 §603.185 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10134 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Credential Persistence: Long-lived credentials should not be stored in ordinary BOOTSTRAP-600 application state. They belong to: secure storage platform credential store hardware-backed storage where available. | 0828 §603.186 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10135 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Storage API: secure_store.put(key, secret) secure_store.get(key) secure_store.delete(key) The storage provider may be platform-native. | 0828 §603.187 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10136 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Storage Provider: Possible providers: Windows credential facilities macOS Keychain iOS Keychain/Secure Enclave Android Keystore Linux secure store Axiom native encrypted store The API remains platform-neutral. | 0828 §603.188 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10137 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Software Fallback: Where no hardware secure store exists, the runtime may use software encryption. It must clearly distinguish: hardware-backed OS-backed software-protected storage. | 0828 §603.189 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10138 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Master Key: The runtime must not hard-code a universal master key. Keys derive from platform/user/application-specific secure sources. | 0828 §603.190 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10139 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Key Rotation: Secure storage supports versioned keys where practical. | 0828 §603.191 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10140 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Credential Deletion: Deleting a credential should invalidate its application reference. Best-effort physical erasure depends on the underlying storage technology. | 0828 §603.192 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10141 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Events: Recommended event IDs: SEC_CAPABILITY_DENIED SEC_CAPABILITY_REVOKED SEC_PERMISSION_CHANGED SEC_SIGNATURE_INVALID SEC_MODULE_REJECTED SEC_AUTH_FAILED SEC_CREDENTIAL_ACCESS SEC_TRUST_FAILED SEC_SANDBOX_VIOLATION SEC_QUOTA_EXCEEDED | 0828 §603.193 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10142 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Event Redaction: Security event payloads must pass through the same secret-protection layer as ordinary diagnostics. | 0828 §603.194 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10143 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Metrics: Optional counters: authorization_denied authentication_failed module_rejected capability_revoked sandbox_denied credential_failures | 0828 §603.195 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10144 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Health: SecurityHealth { trust_status sandbox_status secure_storage_status crypto_status } | 0828 §603.196 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10145 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Self-Test: Optional: security.self_test() may verify: - secure random source; - cryptographic backend; - secure storage; - capability subsystem; - trust metadata. It must not expose secrets. | 0828 §603.197 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10146 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Failure Isolation: If optional security telemetry fails: security enforcement continues Diagnostics must not weaken authorization merely because logging is unavailable. | 0828 §603.198 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10147 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Fail-Closed Operations: For security-critical authorization: unknown must normally behave as: deny unless an explicitly documented policy says otherwise. | 0828 §603.199 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10148 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Fail-Open Exceptions: Fail-open behavior must be explicitly declared and limited to operations where security consequences are acceptable. It must never be an accidental default. | 0828 §603.200 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10149 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Policy: Applications may define: SecurityPolicy { required_signer allowed_modules allowed_capabilities crypto_policy credential_policy } | 0828 §603.201 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10150 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Immutability: Once a security-critical policy is active, ordinary application code cannot silently weaken it. | 0828 §603.202 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10151 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Layers: Policy precedence: platform ↓ deployment ↓ application ↓ resource ↓ operation A lower layer may restrict authority but must not bypass a higher-level denial. | 0828 §603.203 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10152 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Policy Compilation: Static policy should be compiled into compact native structures where possible. | 0828 §603.204 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10153 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Runtime Cost: A capability authorization check should target: O(1) for ordinary capability operations. | 0828 §603.205 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10154 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Metadata: A release executable may contain: application identity publisher identity requested capabilities module requirements security policy hash | 0828 §603.206 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10155 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Fingerprint: The active security policy may expose: security.policy_fingerprint() This integrates with BOOTSTRAP-602 diagnostics. | 0828 §603.207 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10156 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Context Fingerprint: A diagnostic snapshot may contain: security policy fingerprint trust status capability profile without exposing individual secret values. | 0828 §603.208 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10157 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — AI-Friendly Security Metadata: The toolchain should emit machine-readable metadata describing: capability requirements resource boundaries trust requirements module dependencies security policy This allows automated tooling to understand why an operation was denied. | 0828 §603.209 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10158 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Manifest: A deployment manifest should support: security: capabilities: trusted_publishers: trusted_modules: crypto_policy: sandbox: secure_storage: | 0828 §603.210 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10159 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Diff: Tooling should be able to compare two builds: build A capabilities vs build B capabilities and identify added/removed requested authority. | 0828 §603.211 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10160 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax security`: The toolchain should provide: ax security inspect ax security manifest ax security verify ax security capabilities ax security modules | 0828 §603.212 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10161 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax security capabilities`: Outputs: requested granted denied inherited delegated revoked | 0828 §603.213 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10162 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — `ax security verify`: Checks: binary signature module signatures build identity manifest policy dependency integrity | 0828 §603.214 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10163 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Static Capability Analysis: The compiler may determine: function → required capability when capability requirements are explicit. Example: save_document() requires FileWrite | 0828 §603.215 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10164 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Propagation: If: fn save(cap: FileWriteCapability) calls: write_file(cap) the compiler can propagate the requirement. | 0828 §603.216 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10165 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Requirement Graph: The compiler may generate: function ↓ required capability ↓ module ↓ application manifest | 0828 §603.217 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10166 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dead Capability Elimination: If a capability-dependent subsystem is unused, associated runtime code should be removable. | 0828 §603.218 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10167 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Footprint: The toolchain should report: filesystem access network access process access device access credential access JIT access for an executable. | 0828 §603.219 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10168 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Footprint Does Not Equal Runtime Permission: Static analysis describes potential authority. The runtime determines actual granted authority. | 0828 §603.220 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10169 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Sandboxed Build: A build may intentionally restrict its static capability surface. The compiler can reject APIs requiring capabilities outside the declared profile. | 0828 §603.221 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10170 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Injection: At application startup: fn main( fs: FileSystemCapability, net: NetworkCapability ) may receive capabilities explicitly. This makes dependencies visible in the application entry point. | 0828 §603.222 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10171 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dependency Injection Without Framework: No dependency-injection framework is required. Capabilities are ordinary typed parameters. | 0828 §603.223 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10172 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Testing: Tests may inject mock capabilities: FakeFileSystemCapability provided they implement the required restricted interface. | 0828 §603.224 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10173 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Test Isolation: Tests should default to: no network no real credentials temporary filesystem no process spawning unless explicitly enabled. | 0828 §603.225 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10174 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Test Capability: The test runtime may expose synthetic capabilities that cannot affect the real system. | 0828 §603.226 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10175 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Fuzzing: Security-sensitive parsers and capability boundaries should be fuzz-testable without requiring real privileged resources. | 0828 §603.227 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10176 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Deterministic Security Tests: Where practical, permission decisions should be testable deterministically. | 0828 §603.228 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10177 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Error Taxonomy: Core errors: SecurityError { denied unavailable expired revoked invalid_identity invalid_signature trust_failure quota_exceeded sandbox_violation credential_unavailable policy_violation } | 0828 §603.229 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10178 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Error Codes: Security errors have stable numeric IDs for diagnostics and IPC. | 0828 §603.230 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10179 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — ABI Stability: Security error and capability ABI structures require explicit versioning. | 0828 §603.231 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10180 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Platform Adapter Contract: Each platform adapter implements: identity permissions sandbox secure storage crypto randomness process authority filesystem authority network authority code trust where supported. | 0828 §603.232 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10181 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Windows Adapter: Integrates with: - process identity; - ACL/security descriptors; - code signing; - credential facilities; - protected storage where available; - native process/token mechanisms. | 0828 §603.233 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10182 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Linux Adapter: Integrates with: - file permissions; - user/group identity; - namespaces where available; - sandboxing mechanisms; - kernel credential boundaries; - native secure random source. | 0828 §603.234 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10183 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — macOS Adapter: Integrates with: - code signing; - entitlements; - sandbox; - Keychain; - application identity; - platform permission mechanisms. | 0828 §603.235 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10184 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — iOS Adapter: The architecture respects: - application sandbox; - entitlements; - Keychain; - Secure Enclave where available; - platform permission dialogs; - code-signing restrictions. | 0828 §603.236 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10185 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Android Adapter: Integrates with: - application identity; - permissions; - sandbox UID; - Keystore; - package signing; - platform security policy. | 0828 §603.237 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10186 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — WASM Adapter: WASM authority is determined by the host. Axiom capabilities map to host-provided imports/interfaces. No capability is assumed merely because the WASM module exists. | 0828 §603.238 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10187 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cross-Platform Semantic Rule: The same Axiom API should preserve this invariant: operation succeeds only if required capability is valid AND platform policy permits it | 0828 §603.239 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10188 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Platform Differences: The runtime may expose capability state as: supported unsupported restricted granted denied instead of pretending every platform provides identical security features. | 0828 §603.240 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10189 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No False Security: The runtime must not label software-only protection as hardware-backed protection. | 0828 §603.241 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10190 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Claims: Axiom documentation must distinguish: language guarantee runtime guarantee platform guarantee configuration guarantee best effort | 0828 §603.242 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10191 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory Security: Security-sensitive memory APIs should provide: guarded allocation zeroization restricted access optional locking where supported. | 0828 §603.243 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10192 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Allocator: A secure allocator may exist: secure.alloc<T>(count) It is intended for sensitive data, not ordinary application allocations. | 0828 §603.244 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10193 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Allocator Constraints: Secure allocation may be: - slower; - non-movable; - non-swappable; - quota-limited. The application must opt in. | 0828 §603.245 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10194 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Universal Secure Memory Promise: The runtime cannot guarantee physical memory secrecy against a fully privileged operating system/kernel. Documentation must state the trust boundary. | 0828 §603.246 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10195 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trust Boundary: Default trust model: Application ↓ trusts Axiom runtime ↓ trusts Operating system ↓ trusts Hardware Platform security can alter this boundary. | 0828 §603.247 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10196 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hostile Application Code: The capability model assumes application components may be mutually untrusted. This enables future plugin/sandbox architectures. | 0828 §603.248 | GAP |
