| RQ-C11-10197 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Plugin Capability Boundary: A plugin receives: only explicitly granted capabilities not the application's entire authority. | 0828 §603.249 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10198 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Plugin Manifest: Plugins may declare: required capabilities publisher version hash ABI | 0828 §603.250 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10199 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Plugin Approval: The host application determines whether the plugin is acceptable. The runtime enforces the granted capability boundary. | 0828 §603.251 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10200 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Plugin Revocation: A plugin capability can be revoked without necessarily terminating the entire application. | 0828 §603.252 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10201 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Untrusted Data: External data is treated as: data not: trusted code until explicitly validated. | 0828 §603.253 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10202 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trust Conversion: Converting external data into privileged objects requires validation. | 0828 §603.254 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10203 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Input Validation: The runtime provides primitives for: range checking length checking encoding validation schema validation signature validation | 0828 §603.255 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10204 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — UTF-8 Security: Axiom's UTF-8 default must not imply that arbitrary byte sequences are valid text. The runtime distinguishes: Bytes String | 0828 §603.256 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10205 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Invalid UTF-8: Converting bytes to String requires explicit validation or a defined lossy conversion. | 0828 §603.257 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10206 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unicode Normalization: Security-sensitive identifiers may optionally require normalization. The runtime must not silently normalize arbitrary user data. | 0828 §603.258 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10207 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Case Sensitivity: Security-sensitive resource names must respect platform-specific case semantics. The runtime should expose canonical comparison rules. | 0828 §603.259 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10208 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Filename Security: Applications must not assume: same textual path = same resource across platforms. Capability-bound resource handles remain authoritative. | 0828 §603.260 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10209 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Environment Security: BOOTSTRAP-601 environment values are untrusted input unless explicitly declared trusted. | 0828 §603.261 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10210 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Configuration Security: Configuration cannot grant itself capabilities beyond the deployment/platform policy. | 0828 §603.262 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10211 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — CLI Security: Command-line options cannot override mandatory security restrictions. | 0828 §603.263 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10212 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Debug Configuration: A debug flag cannot disable mandatory signature or sandbox enforcement in production. | 0828 §603.264 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10213 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Development Escape Hatch: Development-only bypasses must be: explicit visible build-identifiable non-default | 0828 §603.265 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10214 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Banner: Diagnostic metadata may identify: development security mode when enabled. | 0828 §603.266 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10215 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Production Build Validation: The build tool should warn or fail when production configuration contains: debug bypass trust-all disable-signature-check allow-unsigned-module style settings. | 0828 §603.267 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10216 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Policy Hash: The final executable may contain the hash of the security policy actually compiled into the binary. | 0828 §603.268 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10217 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Mismatch Detection: At startup: runtime policy vs deployment policy must be checked for compatibility. | 0828 §603.269 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10218 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Immutable Startup Security: Mandatory security decisions should occur before untrusted application initialization. | 0828 §603.270 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10219 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Early Attack Surface: The bootstrap sequence should minimize: dynamic loading network access configuration parsing plugin loading before security initialization. | 0828 §603.271 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10220 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Configuration Parsing: BOOTSTRAP-601 configuration files are untrusted input until validated. | 0828 §603.272 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10221 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Manifest Validation: The deployment manifest must be: parsed schema-checked policy-checked integrity-checked where applicable before capabilities are established. | 0828 §603.273 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10222 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Defaults on Parse Failure: Invalid security configuration results in: restricted startup rather than permissive fallback. | 0828 §603.274 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10223 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Startup Graph: Startup: identity ↓ trust verification ↓ manifest validation ↓ platform permissions ↓ capability construction ↓ application initialization | 0828 §603.275 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10224 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Shutdown: Shutdown invalidates or releases: temporary capabilities session credentials IPC channels privileged handles according to their lifecycle. | 0828 §603.276 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10225 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Session Termination: BOOTSTRAP-600 session termination must invalidate session-scoped capabilities. | 0828 §603.277 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10226 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — User Logout: Where applicable: logout ↓ credential/session invalidation ↓ capability revocation | 0828 §603.278 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10227 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Event on Revocation: Capability revocation may generate: security.capability.revoked for diagnostics. | 0828 §603.279 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10228 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash-Time Security Capture: Crash handling may record: security policy fingerprint application identity publisher identity trust state but must not inspect all capabilities or credentials indiscriminately. | 0828 §603.280 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10229 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and Diagnostics Boundary: BOOTSTRAP-603 owns: authority trust identity credential protection BOOTSTRAP-602 owns: recording diagnostic persistence crash reporting | 0828 §603.281 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10230 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and Configuration Boundary: BOOTSTRAP-601 declares: desired deployment configuration BOOTSTRAP-603 decides: security authority actually available | 0828 §603.282 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10231 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and State Boundary: BOOTSTRAP-600 owns: application state BOOTSTRAP-603 owns: security state Only references to security state should enter ordinary application checkpoints. | 0828 §603.283 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10232 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security State: Security state may include: permission status capability revocation trust state credential references policy version | 0828 §603.284 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10233 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Credential References: Application state stores: CredentialId not: raw credential | 0828 §603.285 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10234 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Restore Safety: Restoring an application checkpoint must not automatically restore expired or revoked capabilities. | 0828 §603.286 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10235 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security-Aware Recovery: After crash recovery: application state restored + security state revalidated before privileged operations resume. | 0828 §603.287 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10236 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Replay Protection: Security-sensitive operations must not be replayed merely because application state was restored. | 0828 §603.288 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10237 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Transaction Identity: Security-sensitive transactions may include: TransactionId Nonce SessionId for replay protection. | 0828 §603.289 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10238 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Monotonic Counter: Platforms supporting secure counters may expose them through: secure.counter() for replay-sensitive applications. | 0828 §603.290 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10239 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Atomic Security State: Permission/capability changes should be applied atomically from the application's perspective. | 0828 §603.291 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10240 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Concurrent Revocation: If a capability is revoked concurrently with an operation, the runtime defines whether: operation already authorized may complete. The default rule is: > Revocation prevents subsequent authorization; it does not necessarily cancel an already-authorized kernel operation. | 0828 §603.292 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10241 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Authorization Race: Security-sensitive operations should use atomic platform primitives where available to reduce authorization races. | 0828 §603.293 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10242 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Invariant: At all times: effective authority ⊆ granted authority ⊆ deployment authority ⊆ platform authority | 0828 §603.294 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10243 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Privilege Amplification: No combination of ordinary Axiom APIs may transform: Capability<A> into: Capability<UnrelatedPrivilege> without an explicit trusted boundary. | 0828 §603.295 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10244 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Monotonicity: Capability derivation must satisfy: Authority(child) <= Authority(parent) unless the operation crosses a separately authenticated privilege boundary. | 0828 §603.296 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10245 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Boundary Crossing: Crossing into a privileged subsystem requires: authentication authorization input validation bounded resource use audit event where applicable. | 0828 §603.297 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10246 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Ambient Root Capability: Axiom does not expose: root_capability() to ordinary application code. | 0828 §603.298 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10247 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trusted Runtime Code: Some runtime operations necessarily require elevated native authority. These are isolated inside trusted runtime components. | 0828 §603.299 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10248 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trusted Runtime Surface: The trusted computing base should be kept small. Optional subsystems should remain outside the mandatory security core. | 0828 §603.300 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10249 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Compiler Trust: The compiler is part of the build-time trust boundary. Reproducible builds and signed compiler/toolchain artifacts are outside the mandatory application runtime but supported by the ecosystem. | 0828 §603.301 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10250 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Runtime Self-Identity: The runtime exposes: runtime.identity() including: runtime version ABI build identity security feature set | 0828 §603.302 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10251 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Feature Availability: Applications can query: security.features() to determine platform support. | 0828 §603.303 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10252 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Introspection: Applications may inspect whether a capability is: valid revoked expired restricted but should not be able to extract privileged internal representation. | 0828 §603.304 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10253 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Handle Introspection: A `Handle<T>` should expose only safe metadata: valid type state not raw kernel pointers unless explicitly requested through an unsafe API. | 0828 §603.305 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10254 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unsafe Native Handle Extraction: If required for FFI: unsafe native_handle(handle) must be explicitly marked unsafe. | 0828 §603.306 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10255 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Native Handle Lifetime: The developer is responsible for respecting the ownership contract when using extracted handles. | 0828 §603.307 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10256 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and Memory Model: The security architecture must remain compatible with Axiom's high-performance native memory model. It must not introduce: - mandatory GC; - mandatory borrow checker; - mandatory reference counting; - hidden heap allocations. | 0828 §603.308 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10257 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and Performance: Security checks should use: typed capabilities opaque handles constant-time primitives where required bounded authorization checks rather than pervasive dynamic policy interpretation. | 0828 §603.309 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10258 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Fast Path: After capability validation, hot resource operations may use a compact validated handle. Example: Capability ↓ validate NativeHandle ↓ fast operation | 0828 §603.310 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10259 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Revocation Tradeoff: Instant revocation may require indirection. The runtime may choose: generation counter capability table revocation epoch kernel-backed handle depending on platform. | 0828 §603.311 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10260 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Generation Counters: A capability handle may encode: index generation so stale handles are rejected. | 0828 §603.312 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10261 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Stale Capability: Using a stale capability returns: SecurityError.revoked rather than accessing a reused resource. | 0828 §603.313 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10262 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Resource Identity: The runtime should distinguish: resource identity handle identity capability identity | 0828 §603.314 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10263 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Table: A runtime implementation may maintain: CapabilityTable for resources requiring centralized revocation. | 0828 §603.315 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10264 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Table Performance: Lookup target: O(1) average case. | 0828 §603.316 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10265 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Table Memory: Entries are bounded by configured resource limits. | 0828 §603.317 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10266 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Resource Exhaustion: Failure to create a capability due to table exhaustion returns: SecurityError.quota_exceeded or an explicit resource-exhaustion error. | 0828 §603.318 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10267 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Telemetry: Security metrics must not become an attack vector. High-volume security failures must be rate-limited. | 0828 §603.319 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10268 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Event Flood: If an attacker causes thousands of permission failures: application remains responsive and diagnostic storage remains bounded. | 0828 §603.320 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10269 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Logging Priority: Critical security events may bypass ordinary log filtering while still respecting privacy. | 0828 §603.321 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10270 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Durability: Applications requiring durable security auditing can configure durable storage explicitly. Ordinary application logs do not receive this guarantee automatically. | 0828 §603.322 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10271 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Tamper Evidence: Optional hash chaining: H0 H1 = H(H0 // E1) H2 = H(H1 // E2) ... allows detection of modifications. | 0828 §603.323 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10272 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Key: Tamper-evident audit chains may use a signing key or MAC key stored through secure storage. | 0828 §603.324 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10273 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Audit Verification: Tool: ax security audit verify checks chain integrity. | 0828 §603.325 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10274 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Export: Audit export must preserve: event identity timestamp sequence integrity metadata | 0828 §603.326 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10275 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Automatic Remote Upload: Security audit data is never automatically uploaded by the core runtime. | 0828 §603.327 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10276 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Threat Model: The implementation specification must explicitly document whether it protects against: untrusted application input untrusted plugins untrusted local users malicious modules network attackers compromised dependencies | 0828 §603.328 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10277 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Out of Scope Threats: The core runtime cannot guarantee protection against: fully compromised operating system fully compromised kernel malicious hypervisor physically compromised hardware unless platform-specific trusted hardware establishes such a boundary. | 0828 §603.329 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10278 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Threat Model Metadata: Build documentation may contain: security assumptions trust boundaries platform requirements | 0828 §603.330 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10279 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Review Artifact: The toolchain may generate: .axsecurity containing: capability graph module trust graph security policy resource permissions crypto usage | 0828 §603.331 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10280 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — AI Security Analysis: An AI tool can consume `.axsecurity` to answer: Which function requires network access? Which module can access credentials? Which plugin has filesystem write authority? Which build gained a new capability? without inspecting every source file. | 0828 §603.332 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10281 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Diff: The tool should support: ax security diff old.axsecurity new.axsecurity and identify structural changes. The tool reports facts; it does not assign a security score. | 0828 §603.333 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10282 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Compiler Diagnostics: Examples: SEC001 capability required SEC002 capability unavailable SEC003 secret passed to diagnostic API SEC004 unsigned module SEC005 invalid trust policy SEC006 insecure random source SEC007 unsafe credential conversion SEC008 forbidden privilege escalation SEC009 invalid capability attenuation SEC010 security policy mismatch | 0828 §603.334 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10283 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Compile-Time Secret Protection: The compiler should reject obvious flows: Secret<T> ↓ String ↓ log() unless explicitly overridden through an unsafe security API. | 0828 §603.335 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10284 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Static Taint Metadata: The compiler may track: secret untrusted trusted privileged metadata. This is optional but strongly supported. | 0828 §603.336 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10285 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Untrusted Data: External input may be marked: Untrusted<T> and validated into: Trusted<T> when a validator succeeds. | 0828 §603.337 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10286 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trusted Conversion: Example: let username = validate_username(input)? returns a restricted validated type. | 0828 §603.338 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10287 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Taint Propagation: The compiler may propagate security metadata through: assignment function parameters struct fields serialization FFI logging | 0828 §603.339 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10288 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Taint Does Not Replace Authorization: A value being marked `Trusted<T>` does not grant resource capabilities. | 0828 §603.340 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10289 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Metadata Cost: Security metadata should be erased from runtime representations whenever it is compile-time-only. | 0828 §603.341 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10290 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Zero Runtime Cost Security Types: Where possible: Trusted<T> Untrusted<T> Secret<T> should have the same physical representation as `T`, while enforcing restrictions through the compiler. | 0828 §603.342 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10291 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Runtime Secret Protection: Runtime protection remains necessary when secrets cross dynamic/native boundaries. | 0828 §603.343 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10292 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Serialization: Secrets cannot be serialized through generic serializers without an explicit security policy. | 0828 §603.344 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10293 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secret Persistence: `Secret<T>` does not imply persistence. Secure storage is a separate subsystem. | 0828 §603.345 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10294 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Delete: Secure deletion semantics are platform-dependent. The API must distinguish: logical delete best-effort overwrite secure-store destruction | 0828 §603.346 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10295 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No False Erasure Guarantee: Axiom must not promise physical deletion on storage systems where the underlying medium cannot provide it. | 0828 §603.347 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10296 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Serialization: Capabilities generally cannot be serialized directly. Instead: capability ↓ explicit transferable token may be used. | 0828 §603.348 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10297 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Token: Transfer tokens must be: opaque bounded expiring where appropriate single-use where appropriate | 0828 §603.349 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10298 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Token Binding: A transfer token may be bound to: recipient identity session process resource expiration | 0828 §603.350 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10299 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Replay Prevention: Single-use security tokens must contain replay-protection state. | 0828 §603.351 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10300 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure IPC Token Exchange: Token exchange: sender ↓ authenticate receiver ↓ verify token ↓ construct capability | 0828 §603.352 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10301 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Delegation Graph: The runtime may represent: root capability ↓ attenuated capability ↓ delegated capability for audit purposes. | 0828 §603.353 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10302 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Delegation Constraint: Delegated authority cannot exceed the authority of the delegating capability. | 0828 §603.354 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10303 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Context Snapshot: A diagnostic snapshot may record the identity of the security context but not its secret internal representation. | 0828 §603.355 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10304 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Context Recovery: After process restart, capability objects are recreated from platform authorization rather than blindly restored from serialized memory. | 0828 §603.356 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10305 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash Recovery Security Rule: A restored application checkpoint cannot resurrect: revoked permission expired credential expired capability invalid trust state | 0828 §603.357 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10306 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Application Update Security: State migration across versions must not automatically transfer obsolete privileged capabilities. | 0828 §603.358 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10307 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Migration: When an application updates: old capability model ↓ policy reconciliation ↓ new capability model | 0828 §603.359 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10308 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Version: Security policy has a version identifier. | 0828 §603.360 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10309 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Policy Migration: Breaking security-policy changes require explicit migration logic. | 0828 §603.361 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10310 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Defaults During Migration: If migration fails: restricted mode rather than unrestricted mode. | 0828 §603.362 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10311 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Emergency Recovery: Applications may expose a recovery mode with minimal authority: read diagnostics repair configuration restore state but no unnecessary network/process/device authority. | 0828 §603.363 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10312 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Recovery Capability: Recovery mode receives a deliberately reduced capability set. | 0828 §603.364 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10313 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Safe Mode: Axiom may provide: application.safe_mode() at the lifecycle layer. BOOTSTRAP-603 supplies the security profile. | 0828 §603.365 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10314 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Safe Mode Diagnostics: Safe mode integrates with BOOTSTRAP-602 so that security failures remain diagnosable. | 0828 §603.366 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10315 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Platform Permission Prompt: Axiom must not bypass platform permission dialogs. | 0828 §603.367 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10316 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Permission UX: User-facing permission explanations belong to the application/UI layer. The security runtime exposes machine-readable permission reasons. | 0828 §603.368 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10317 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Permission Reason: Example: PermissionReason.camera.capture | 0828 §603.369 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10318 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Permission Minimization: The compiler/toolchain should be able to determine which declared capabilities are actually referenced. | 0828 §603.370 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10319 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unused Capability Warning: If a manifest requests a capability never used by the executable: warning: unused capability request | 0828 §603.371 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10320 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Capability Reduction: The deployment tool may generate a minimized manifest containing only required capabilities. | 0828 §603.372 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10321 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dynamic Capability Use: Dynamic plugins may prevent complete static capability analysis. The tool must mark such requirements as dynamic rather than pretending certainty. | 0828 §603.373 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10322 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Dynamic Loading Warning: Applications using unrestricted dynamic module discovery should receive an explicit security diagnostic. | 0828 §603.374 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10323 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Boundary Documentation: Every native platform adapter must document: what it guarantees what it delegates what it cannot guarantee | 0828 §603.375 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10324 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cross-Compilation: Security metadata must remain valid when targeting another platform. | 0828 §603.376 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10325 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Unsupported Capability: When a target lacks a capability: compile-time error if required statically, or: unsupported at runtime if dynamically optional. | 0828 §603.377 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10326 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Silent Emulation: A capability must not silently degrade into a weaker security mechanism. | 0828 §603.378 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10327 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crypto Backend: Axiom may have a native crypto backend selected per target. The public API remains stable. | 0828 §603.379 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10328 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Backend Independence: Applications should not depend directly on the internal cryptographic implementation. | 0828 §603.380 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10329 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Constant-Time Native Primitives: Security-critical primitive implementations should avoid data-dependent branches where algorithmically required. | 0828 §603.381 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10330 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Side-Channel Documentation: The runtime documentation must state which side-channel protections are guaranteed and which depend on the platform. | 0828 §603.382 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10331 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Hardware Acceleration: Crypto operations may use: CPU instructions hardware security modules platform crypto APIs without changing the public API. | 0828 §603.383 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10332 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — CPU Feature Detection: The runtime may select accelerated crypto implementations after securely determining CPU features. | 0828 §603.384 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10333 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Unsafe Fallback: A hardware-accelerated implementation may fall back to a compatible software implementation, but not to an insecure algorithm merely because acceleration is unavailable. | 0828 §603.385 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10334 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Entropy Failure: If secure randomness is unavailable: secure.random() must fail. It must not silently fall back to predictable randomness. | 0828 §603.386 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10335 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Secure Time: Security protocols requiring trusted time should use platform facilities where available. | 0828 §603.387 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10336 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Time-Based Authorization: Expiration checks must define behavior if the system clock moves backward or forward unexpectedly. | 0828 §603.388 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10337 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Monotonic Expiration: Where practical, short-lived capabilities should use monotonic deadlines. | 0828 §603.389 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10338 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Performance Target: Capability checks should target: O(1) and minimal allocations. | 0828 §603.390 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10339 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cryptographic Performance: The runtime should expose hardware-accelerated implementations where available without changing semantics. | 0828 §603.391 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10340 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Binary Size: Unused cryptographic algorithms and security providers should be dead-strippable. | 0828 §603.392 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10341 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Minimal Security Runtime: A minimal native application should be able to include only: identity capability core secure randomness required platform security without pulling the entire diagnostics/security ecosystem. | 0828 §603.393 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10342 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Mandatory GC: Security types must not require garbage collection. | 0828 §603.394 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10343 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Mandatory Reference Counting: Security handles use deterministic ownership/lifetime semantics. Reference counting may be used internally where useful but is not a language requirement. | 0828 §603.395 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10344 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Mandatory Borrow Checker: Capability safety is achieved through: opaque types ownership capability construction rules runtime validation rather than requiring a universal borrow-checking model. | 0828 §603.396 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10345 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and Flat Memory: The security subsystem remains compatible with Axiom's native memory architecture. Privileged resources remain represented as opaque handles rather than exposing raw security-sensitive memory addresses. | 0828 §603.397 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10346 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security and Struct-Oriented Design: Security abstractions use structs/traits rather than mandatory classes. Example: struct FileCapability { handle: Handle<FileAuthority> } fn read(cap: FileCapability, path: Path) | 0828 §603.398 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10347 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Override Compatibility: Platform-specific security adapters may override trait implementations without introducing class inheritance. | 0828 §603.399 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10348 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Trait Example: trait Capability { fn is_valid(self) -> bool fn revoke(self) } Concrete platform types implement the trait. | 0828 §603.400 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10349 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — No Virtual Security Dependency: Performance-sensitive authorization paths should prefer static dispatch. Dynamic dispatch is permitted where plugin architecture requires it. | 0828 §603.401 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10350 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Compile-Time Security Graph: The compiler may construct: module ↓ function ↓ capability ↓ resource graphs. | 0828 §603.402 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10351 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Runtime Security Graph: The runtime tracks dynamic: grant delegation revocation expiration relationships where required. | 0828 §603.403 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10352 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Graph Persistence: Only metadata necessary for recovery/audit is persisted. Raw capability internals are not serialized into ordinary application state. | 0828 §603.404 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10353 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Acceptance Criteria: BOOTSTRAP-603 is complete when the Axiom implementation demonstrates: ### Capability - typed capabilities; - non-forgeable privileged authority; - attenuation; - revocation; - expiration; - delegation; - quotas; - explicit inheritance. ### Identity - application identity; - build identity; - publisher identity; - module identity; - peer identity. ### Trust - signature verification; - module verification; - policy enforcement; - trust-state reporting. ### Secrets - opaque secret types; - secure storage; - zeroization; - secret-safe diagnostics; - hardware-backed integration where available. ### Cryptography - secure random; - hashes; - MAC; - KDF; - AEAD; - signatures; - typed keys; - constant-time comparison. ### Platform - Windows; - Linux; - macOS; - iOS; - Android; - WASM. ### Isolation - sandbox integration; - process capability; - filesystem capability; - network capability; - device capability; - IPC capability. ### Compiler - static capability analysis; - capability metadata; - security diagnostics; - capability dead stripping; - AI-readable security graph. ### Runtime - O(1)-target authorization; - no mandatory GC; - no mandatory borrow checker; - deterministic resource cleanup; - bounded security metadata. | 0828 §603.405 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10354 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Required Compiler/Runtime Components: Logical components: axiom.security.core axiom.security.capability axiom.security.identity axiom.security.trust axiom.security.crypto axiom.security.secrets axiom.security.storage axiom.security.ipc axiom.security.sandbox axiom.security.audit They need not become separate binaries. | 0828 §603.406 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10355 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Required Tooling: The Axiom toolchain should provide: ax security inspect ax security verify ax security capabilities ax security diff ax security audit ax security modules | 0828 §603.407 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10356 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Artifact: The toolchain should generate: .axsecurity containing machine-readable: capability graph identity trust requirements module graph policy crypto usage security boundaries | 0828 §603.408 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10357 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — AI-Agent Consumption: An AI coding agent should be able to inspect `.axsecurity` and determine: why an API requires authority which module owns that authority which caller supplied it whether a capability is static or dynamic which deployment permission is missing without scanning the complete source tree. | 0828 §603.409 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10358 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security Architecture Invariants: The following invariants are mandatory: 1. Authority is explicit. 2. Authority cannot increase through attenuation. 3. Privileged capabilities cannot be forged by ordinary code. 4. Unknown security state fails closed by default. 5. Secrets cannot enter ordinary diagnostics accidentally. 6. Revoked authority cannot be used for new operations. 7. Restored state cannot resurrect revoked authority. 8. Dynamic modules do not automatically become trusted. 9. Secure randomness never silently falls back to predictable randomness. 10. Security failures cannot silently downgrade to insecure behavior. 11. Security enforcement does not depend on diagnostics availability. 12. Security metadata does not require GC. 13. Platform differences remain explicit. 14. The application cannot grant itself platform authority. 15. The runtime does not require a third-party security service. | 0828 §603.410 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10359 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Architectural Result: After BOOTSTRAP-603, the Axiom native runtime has the following security foundation: APPLICATION │ ┌───────┴───────┐ ▼               ▼ IDENTITY         STATE 600 │ ▼ TRUST │ ▼ CAPABILITY CORE ┌──────┼──────┐ ▼      ▼      ▼ FILE    NETWORK  IPC │      │      │ └──────┼──────┘ ▼ SECURE HANDLES │ ┌─────────┼─────────┐ ▼         ▼         ▼ CRYPTO    SECRETS   SANDBOX │         │         │ └─────────┼─────────┘ ▼ SECURITY AUDIT │ ▼ BOOTSTRAP-602 The three preceding bootstrap layers now form a coherent native application foundation: 600 = state / session / recovery 601 = configuration / environment / deployment 602 = diagnostics / crash / observability 603 = identity / authority / trust / security | 0828 §603.411 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10360 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Task Completion: **BOOTSTRAP-603 is complete.** The specification establishes: - capability-based security; - explicit authority; - capability attenuation; - capability revocation; - identity and trust; - secure handles; - secure storage; - secret protection; - cryptographic primitives; - secure randomness; - sandbox integration; - IPC security; - module trust; - code-signing integration; - privilege separation; - child-process security; - secure update foundations; - static capability analysis; - AI-readable security metadata; - platform-specific security adapters; - deterministic resource ownership; - compatibility with Axiom's native/high-performance memory model; - no mandatory GC; - no mandatory borrow checker; - no mandatory third-party security runtime. **Next task: `BOOTSTRAP-604 — NATIVE APPLICATION RESOURCE, MEMORY, CPU, GPU & ENERGY GOVERNANCE RUNTIME 5.0`** .: | 0828 §603.412 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10361 | ecosystem | post-v1 | Mục tiêu: BOOTSTRAP-602 định nghĩa hệ thống: - structured logging; - diagnostics; - tracing; - metrics; - health/status; - crash handling; - panic/fatal error reporting; - native stack capture; - crash artifact; - minidump/core-dump abstraction; - symbolization; - diagnostic context; - correlation ID; - bounded diagnostic buffers; - crash-safe emergency logging; - log rotation; - diagnostic redaction; - build/config/state correlation; - local và production observability. Mục tiêu chính: > Một ứng dụng Axiom native phải có khả năng tự quan sát, tự chẩn đoán và tạo artifact đủ để điều tra lỗi mà không bắt buộc phụ thuộc vào một logging/telemetry framework bên thứ ba. BOOTSTRAP-602 không biến Axiom runtime thành một monitoring platform. Nó chỉ cung cấp **primitive native, deterministic và composable** để application hoặc framework phía trên xây dựng hệ thống observability. | 0829 §602.0 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10362 | ecosystem | post-v1 | Nguyên tắc thiết kế: Hệ thống phải tuân thủ: 1. native-first; 2. zero/minimal dependency; 3. deterministic; 4. bounded memory; 5. thread-safe; 6. low overhead; 7. crash-safe ở mức có thể; 8. không ghi secret; 9. không block application khi logging bình thường; 10. không làm crash handler phụ thuộc vào allocator; 11. không yêu cầu network; 12. không yêu cầu daemon bên ngoài; 13. có thể disable hoàn toàn; 14. có thể compile-time eliminate log; 15. hỗ trợ Unicode UTF-8; 16. giữ nguyên build identity; 17. liên kết được với configuration fingerprint; 18. liên kết được với application state/checkpoint; 19. có thể symbolicate sau khi process đã chết. | 0829 §602.1 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10363 | ecosystem | post-v1 | Phạm vi: BOOTSTRAP-602 gồm: Logging Diagnostics Tracing Metrics Health Crash handling Panic/fatal handling Stack capture Crash artifacts Symbolization metadata Diagnostic context Correlation Redaction Log sinks Crash-safe emergency buffer Runtime diagnostics API Không gồm: Remote monitoring service Cloud backend Third-party APM Distributed database Analytics platform Log search server Dashboard UI Các thành phần này có thể được xây dựng ở layer cao hơn. | 0829 §602.2 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-10365 | ecosystem | post-v1 | Logging model: Axiom logging không phải string-printing đơn thuần. Primitive chính: log(level, event, fields...) Ví dụ: log.info("server.started", port = 8080, workers = 8) Không yêu cầu format string runtime nếu compiler có thể tạo structured event trực tiếp. | 0829 §602.4 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10366 | ecosystem | post-v1 | Log levels: Core levels: trace debug info notice warn error fatal Semantic: trace  = extremely detailed execution information debug  = developer diagnostics info   = normal lifecycle information notice = significant normal state transition warn   = abnormal but recoverable condition error  = operation failed fatal  = process cannot safely continue | 0829 §602.5 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10367 | ecosystem | post-v1 | Compile-time log filtering: Compiler/runtime phải cho phép: @log_level("info") Khi build production: trace → removed debug → removed info  → retained notice → retained warn → retained error → retained fatal → retained Code bị loại bỏ phải càng gần zero-cost càng tốt. Không được evaluate argument nếu statement đã bị compile-time eliminated. Ví dụ: debug(expensive_diagnostic()) Nếu `debug` bị disable: expensive_diagnostic() không được thực thi. | 0829 §602.6 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10368 | ecosystem | post-v1 | Runtime log filtering: Compile-time filtering không thay thế runtime filtering. Có thể cấu hình: default = info network = debug database = warn graphics = error Lookup category phải có overhead thấp. | 0829 §602.7 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10369 | ecosystem | post-v1 | Event identity: Mỗi structured event có: event_id category level timestamp thread_id process_id message fields context `event_id` nên là stable identifier. Ví dụ: APP.SERVER.STARTED APP.DB.CONNECTION_FAILED APP.CONFIG.RELOAD_FAILED | 0829 §602.8 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-10861 | ecosystem | post-v1 | Core invariant summary: BOOTSTRAP-602 phải bảo đảm: 1. Logging is structured. 2. Disabled logging is near-zero cost. 3. Diagnostic memory is bounded. 4. Crash handling does not depend on normal application lifecycle. 5. Crash artifacts are versioned. 6. Stack/build identity are preserved. 7. Secrets are never emitted by default. 8. Config identity links to BOOTSTRAP-601. 9. State/checkpoint identity links to BOOTSTRAP-600. 10. No mandatory network service exists. 11. No mandatory third-party observability library exists. 12. Platform differences are isolated behind native backends. 13. Runtime can degrade gracefully. 14. Diagnostic failures do not normally crash the application. 15. Full observability can be stripped from minimal binaries. | 0829 §602.500 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10862 | ecosystem | post-v1 | Acceptance criteria: BOOTSTRAP-602 được coi là hoàn thành khi implementation có thể chứng minh: ### Logging - [ ] structured events; - [ ] levels; - [ ] categories; - [ ] compile-time elimination; - [ ] runtime filtering; - [ ] sync/async sinks; - [ ] bounded queues; - [ ] rotation; - [ ] redaction. ### Diagnostics - [ ] context; - [ ] correlation IDs; - [ ] metrics; - [ ] tracing; - [ ] health; - [ ] snapshots; - [ ] runtime statistics. ### Crash - [ ] panic; - [ ] fatal; - [ ] native exception capture; - [ ] stack capture; - [ ] registers where supported; - [ ] module inventory; - [ ] crash artifact; - [ ] emergency buffer; - [ ] crash recursion guard. ### Tooling - [ ] `.axcrash` reader; - [ ] symbolization; - [ ] build ID matching; - [ ] diagnostic manifest; - [ ] human-readable report; - [ ] machine-readable report. ### Security - [ ] secret redaction; - [ ] bounded attachments; - [ ] path safety; - [ ] no implicit telemetry; - [ ] no hidden network; - [ ] privacy policies. ### Performance - [ ] disabled log near-zero cost; - [ ] bounded memory; - [ ] no mandatory diagnostic thread; - [ ] no mandatory heap; - [ ] dead stripping; - [ ] minimal runtime profile. ### Integration - [ ] BOOTSTRAP-600 checkpoint linkage; - [ ] BOOTSTRAP-601 config fingerprint linkage; - [ ] deployment/build identity; - [ ] native platform backends. | 0829 §602.501 | GAP |

Diagnostic events. 3. Runtime diagnostics. 4. Lightweight tracing. 5. Correlation/context propagation. 6. Assertion and panic diagnostics. 7. Unhandled exception/fault capture. 8. Crash artifact generation. 9. Stack trace capture. 10. Symbolization. 11. Emergency crash buffer. 12. Health/status diagnostics. 13. Runtime performance counters. 14. Integration với BOOTSTRAP-600 state/runtime lifecycle. 15. Integration với BOOTSTRAP-601 configuration/deployment. 16. Local-first operation. 17. Deterministic machine-readable output. 18. Bounded memory usage. 19. Minimal disabled-path overhead. 20. Không phụ thuộc third-party logging/crash framework. Thiết kế phải phù hợp với mục tiêu Axiom: > Diagnostics phải mạnh khi cần nhưng gần như biến mất khỏi executable khi ứng dụng không sử dụng chúng. | 0830 §602.0 | GAP |

Platform layer chỉ nằm dưới abstraction. | 0830 §602.1 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-10872 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic levels: Axiom định nghĩa: TRACE DEBUG INFO NOTICE WARN ERROR FATAL Thứ tự: TRACE < DEBUG < INFO < NOTICE < WARN < ERROR < FATAL Mỗi logger có threshold. Ví dụ: log.debug("parser", "token accepted") Nếu threshold là `INFO`, compiler/runtime phải loại bỏ tối đa chi phí không cần thiết. | 0830 §602.4 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10873 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Compile-time elimination: Axiom hỗ trợ: diagnostics.level = info Compiler có thể loại bỏ: TRACE DEBUG khỏi binary nếu không cần runtime override. Ví dụ: log.debug("network", expensive_debug_value()) Không được phép gọi: expensive_debug_value() nếu DEBUG đã bị compile-time elimination. | 0830 §602.5 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10874 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Lazy diagnostic arguments: API nên hỗ trợ: log.debug("parser") { "token={token} ast={dump_ast(ast)}" } Closure/block chỉ được thực thi khi event enabled. Compiler có thể lower thành: if logger.enabled(DEBUG): evaluate block | 0830 §602.6 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-10877 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Event definition: Ví dụ: event ParserFailed = 0x120001 Compiler tạo metadata: event_id name category severity source module Metadata có thể được strip trong release build. | 0830 §602.9 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10878 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Event categories: Category là string hoặc compile-time symbol: core memory io network graphics parser compiler application security database Khuyến nghị dùng interned IDs thay vì heap string. | 0830 §602.10 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10879 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Message model: Axiom hỗ trợ: log.info("server", "Listening on {port}") nhưng runtime ưu tiên structured representation: event = SERVER_STARTED fields: port = 8080 Message text là presentation layer. | 0830 §602.11 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10880 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Structured logging format: Diagnostic record canonical: { timestamp, severity, event, category, fields, source, thread, process, context, trace } JSON không phải internal representation bắt buộc. JSON chỉ là output encoder. | 0830 §602.12 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10881 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Binary internal event: Internal event nên dùng binary layout: Header timestamp severity event_id flags payload_size Context thread_id process_id trace_id span_id Payload Mục tiêu: - cache-friendly - append-only - không allocation - dễ serialize - crash-safe hơn text. | 0830 §602.13 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10882 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Event ownership: Diagnostic event sau khi commit vào queue phải độc lập với lifetime của application object. Không lưu raw pointer tới object trong event. | RQ-C11-10883 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Field types: Các field primitive được hỗ trợ: bool i8/i16/i32/i64 u8/u16/u32/u64 f32/f64 char string bytes enum duration timestamp path UUID-like ID source location | 0830 §602.15 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-10888 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Runtime logger configuration: Threshold có thể thay đổi runtime: diagnostics.set_level("network", DEBUG) Update phải atomic. Existing events không bị corrupt. | 0830 §602.20 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-10890 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Console sink: Console sink hỗ trợ: human readable JSON compact colored terminal plain terminal Color phải tự động disable khi output không phải terminal. | 0830 §602.22 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10891 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — File sink: File sink hỗ trợ: append rotation size limit time rotation retention count flush policy | 0830 §602.23 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-10893 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash-safe file handling: File logger không được là dependency bắt buộc của crash handler. Crash handler chỉ sử dụng: emergency buffer và minimal OS write primitive. | 0830 §602.25 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-10895 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Ring buffer: Diagnostic core phải hỗ trợ bounded ring buffer. Ví dụ: capacity = N events Khi đầy: drop oldest hoặc policy configurable: drop_oldest drop_newest block Default: drop_oldest | 0830 §602.27 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10896 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Emergency ring buffer: Ngoài normal ring buffer có: EmergencyDiagnosticBuffer Đặc điểm: - preallocated - bounded - no heap allocation - no locks nếu có thể - usable during fatal failure. | 0830 §602.28 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10897 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash buffer: Crash buffer giữ các event gần nhất: last N diagnostic events Khi crash: crash report + recent diagnostic events Điều này rất quan trọng để biết chuyện gì xảy ra ngay trước fault. | 0830 §602.29 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-10898 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Producer path: Normal event path: application ↓ enabled? ↓ encode ↓ ring buffer ↓ worker ↓ sink Không được: application ↓ format string ↓ filesystem trên hot path mặc định. | 0830 §602.30 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-11245 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — String interning: Interning must be bounded. Never allow unbounded attacker-controlled string table. | 0830 §602.377 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11246 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Attacker-controlled logging: Application may log user input. Therefore: max string length max field count max event size must be enforced. | 0830 §602.378 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11247 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Log injection: Human text sinks must escape: newline control characters terminal escape sequences when configured for security-safe output. | 0830 §602.379 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-11251 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Event rate limiting: Optional: max events/sec/category | 0830 §602.383 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11252 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Rate limit algorithm: A simple token bucket or equivalent bounded algorithm is sufficient. | 0830 §602.384 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11253 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Rate-limit diagnostics: Dropped due to rate limit: rate_limited_events counter. | 0830 §602.385 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-11255 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Sampling vs rate limit: Sampling chooses events statistically/policy-wise. Rate limiting enforces resource bound. They are separate mechanisms. | 0830 §602.387 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11256 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Error prioritization: Errors should not necessarily be dropped because debug traffic is high. Separate priority queues may be supported. | 0830 §602.388 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11257 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Queue architecture: Possible: high priority ring normal ring High priority bounded separately. | 0830 §602.389 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-11259 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Logger ordering: If multiple queues are used, exact cross-priority ordering is not guaranteed unless timestamp/sequence number is included. | 0830 §602.391 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-11261 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Atomic sequence: Use atomic increment only if multi-thread global ordering is needed. Otherwise thread-local sequence may be sufficient. | 0830 §602.393 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11262 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Global ordering semantics: Global event sequence gives total order of enqueue operations, not necessarily wall-clock execution order. | 0830 §602.394 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-11264 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trace/span clock: Span duration uses monotonic clock. | 0830 §602.396 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-11266 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic state machine: Global state: UNINITIALIZED EARLY RUNNING DEGRADED SHUTTING_DOWN STOPPED CRASHING | 0830 §602.398 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11267 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — State transition invariants: Illegal transitions must be rejected or ignored safely. | 0830 §602.399 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11268 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Degraded state: Diagnostics enters DEGRADED if: sink unavailable worker failed disk unavailable Application continues. | 0830 §602.400 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11269 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash state: Once: CRASHING normal diagnostic APIs are disabled or redirected. | 0830 §602.401 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11270 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Emergency writer: Emergency writer supports only: fixed buffer minimal formatting platform write | 0830 §602.402 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11271 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Emergency formatting: Allowed primitives: integer hex enum fixed string address | 0830 §602.403 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11272 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Emergency string limits: All strings bounded. | 0830 §602.404 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11273 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Address formatting: Pointer/address formatting must not dereference memory. | 0830 §602.405 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11274 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Memory probing: Crash handler must not attempt arbitrary memory probing. | 0830 §602.406 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11275 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Stack probing: Only platform-safe stack capture mechanism. | 0830 §602.407 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-11278 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Instruction address: Capture: instruction_pointer | 0830 §602.410 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11279 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Access type: Where available: read write execute unknown | 0830 §602.411 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-11282 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cross-platform normalization: Normalization must not erase important platform-specific information. | 0830 §602.414 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11283 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Crash artifact privacy levels: minimal standard diagnostic | 0830 §602.415 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11284 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Minimal crash artifact: Contains: build platform fault instruction pointer stack | 0830 §602.416 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11285 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Standard crash artifact: Adds: threads modules recent events runtime counters | 0830 §602.417 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-11295 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Diagnostic history: Runtime history bounded by ring buffers. | 0830 §602.427 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-11371 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Cross-platform test matrix: Targets: Windows x64 Linux x64 Linux ARM64 macOS ARM64 iOS ARM64 Android ARM64 WASM Platform không hỗ trợ feature phải pass bằng: capability unavailable không phải runtime crash. | 0830 §602.503 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11372 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Performance acceptance: Benchmarks phải chứng minh: 1. Disabled logs gần như không có overhead. 2. Enabled async logging không serialize toàn application. 3. Ring buffer bounded. 4. No unbounded allocation. 5. Crash path không phụ thuộc normal heap. 6. Diagnostics có thể được linker loại bỏ. 7. Minimal profile có footprint nhỏ. Exact numerical thresholds được freeze sau benchmark prototype thực tế thay vì áp đặt số tùy ý trước khi có implementation. | 0830 §602.504 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-11379 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Mục tiêu: BOOTSTRAP-603 định nghĩa security foundation của Axiom native runtime. Subsystem phải cung cấp: 1. Security boundary. 2. Capability-based access control. 3. Permission model. 4. Privilege separation. 5. Resource authority. 6. Process/module trust boundaries. 7. Sandboxing integration. 8. Secret access control. 9. File/network/device capabilities. 10. Native OS permission mapping. 11. Runtime capability attenuation. 12. Secure defaults. 13. Explicit privilege escalation. 14. Capability inspection. 15. Audit integration. 16. Secure IPC boundary. 17. Plugin/module isolation. 18. Crash-safe security behavior. 19. Compiler/linker security metadata. 20. Minimal overhead when security features are unused. Core principle: > **Code chỉ có quyền làm những gì capability của nó cho phép.** | 0831 §603.0 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11380 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security architecture: Mô hình tổng quát: Application ↓ Axiom Security API ↓ Capability Runtime ├── Capability Registry ├── Permission Resolver ├── Policy Engine ├── Trust Boundary ├── Resource Guards └── Audit Hooks ↓ Platform Security Adapter ↓ Windows / Linux / macOS / iOS / Android / WASM | 0831 §603.1 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11381 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security boundary: Security boundary là nơi code không còn được mặc định tin tưởng lẫn nhau. Boundary có thể nằm giữa: process module plugin sandbox IPC peer external resource | 0831 §603.2 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11382 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Trusted Computing Base: Axiom security TCB tối thiểu: kernel / OS Axiom loader Axiom runtime security core platform security adapter Application code không thuộc TCB. | 0831 §603.3 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11383 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Không biến toàn runtime thành TCB: Logging, GUI, application framework và business library không được mặc định trở thành security authority. | 0831 §603.4 | GAP |

| RQ-C11-11680 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Fuzzing: Security parsers should be fuzzed: policy parser manifest parser capability metadata parser IPC decoder artifact decoder | 0831 §603.301 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11681 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Property tests: Required properties: attenuation never increases authority revocation eventually invalidates new operations policy deny cannot become allow through cache capability serialization cannot recreate authority | 0831 §603.302 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11682 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Concurrency tests: Test: concurrent grant concurrent revoke policy reload resource use task spawn | 0831 §603.303 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11683 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Race detection: Runtime implementation should be testable with race/thread sanitization where available. | 0831 §603.304 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11684 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Failure injection: Inject: policy load failure OS permission failure handle duplication failure sandbox query failure memory allocation failure | 0831 §603.305 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11685 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security logging: Every security denial can optionally produce BOOTSTRAP-602 event. | 0831 §603.306 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11686 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security logging overhead: Disabled audit/security logging must remain cheap. | 0831 §603.307 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11687 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Security emergency path: If security subsystem itself faults: deny privileged operation and emit minimal diagnostic. | 0831 §603.308 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11688 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Fail-closed invariant: For security decision uncertainty: unknown → deny in hardened mode. | 0831 §603.309 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11689 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Platform failure: If OS security API returns unexpected error: SecurityUnavailable rather than treating it as granted. | 0831 §603.310 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11690 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Compatibility exception: Legacy/native profile may expose direct OS errors where required. | 0831 §603.311 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11691 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Error mapping: Platform errors map to: PermissionDenied NotFound NotSupported Revoked ResourceLimit SecurityUnavailable while preserving platform code. | 0831 §603.312 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11692 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — Error detail: Detailed platform code may be available to privileged diagnostics tooling. | 0831 §603.313 | GAP |
| RQ-C11-11693 | ecosystem | post-v1 | — User-facing security errors: Messages should explain: operation required authority denial category without exposing policy secrets. | 0831 §603.314 | GAP |
